# TomoKV — project context for codex

Prepend this to every codex prompt. It is the shared background; each prompt then states its own scope.
Written 2026-09-07. Baseline commit `78c3e5391` (`origin/cpp`), full gate 344/344.

## What it is

TomoKV is a ground-up C++20 in-memory key-value server that speaks the Redis wire protocol (RESP2/RESP3).
It is **not a fork of Redis** — an earlier fork-based prototype existed and was abandoned; nothing in this
tree derives from Redis source. It implements **243 registered commands**. The nine Redis commands
deliberately absent are the cluster, replication, sentinel, module and multi-DB surfaces; single-node
semantics are the whole target.

It is a research system. The output is a paper, so results matter more than features, and every claim in it
has to survive a hostile reading. Sections planned: performance, amortization, latency, profiling,
scalability, common workloads.

## Architecture

**Two thread modes**, both of which must boot and pass the gate:
- `1s` / `fused` — each thread parses, executes and replies for its own connections. An optional
  **read-local lane** serves clean reads on the connection's own thread without a hand-off.
- `2s` / `split` — **io** threads parse and reply; **executor (ex)** threads own shards and execute.
  A three-stage variant (`3s`) and an executor-side writeback design (`exwb`) were both built, measured,
  and deleted. Do not propose either.

**Sharding and ownership.** Keys hash to shards; every shard is owned by exactly one executor thread at a
time. Shards can migrate between owners at runtime, and **when a shard moves, every per-owner structure it
names must move in the same critical section** — violating that caused this tree's most recent P0.

**Ordering ring (`rob`).** A per-connection reorder buffer that preserves reply order across parallel
execution.

**Atomics.** Multi-key atomicity uses group-scoped epoch-MVCC. Cross-shard commands use scatter-gather.
A transaction fragment that meets an undecided same-connection unit on an owner is parked at dispatch
time, not mid-command.

**Flip.** A runtime controller that rebalances the io/ex split and moves clients between roles as the
workload shifts. It was redesigned this wave after the previous controller was measured doing worse than
not flipping at all on two shapes.

**Load balancing.** Key-affine and client-affine balancing (`--key-lb`, `--client-lb`), both default on.

Networking is io_uring; the allocator is jemalloc.

## Non-negotiable correctness laws

Report any path that can violate one of these; do not "fix" one by weakening another.
- Single-owner writes.
- Reads are never obstructed by writes: immutable replacement plus QSBR. **No reader retries and no
  seqlocks on the per-operation path.**
- In-place overwrite is banned while the read-local lane is armed.
- Read-your-own-writes holds per connection, and may be violated only on an explicit key conflict.
- Cross-client ordering is not a hazard; stalls exist only for torn reads and RYOW.
- Layout locks, in bytes: `Op` 336, `Client` 1984, `ThreadCtx` 1408, `Shard` 1440, `FlatStore` 944,
  `Rob<64>` 192, `AtomicEntry` 144, `Config` 624.
- Both thread modes boot. Main commands carry zero regression. One file per feature.

## The box

A single AMD EPYC 9754 (Bergamo): 128 cores, 256 threads, 8 CCD × 16 cores, each CCD 2 CCX × 8 cores with
16 MB L3 — 16 L3 domains, NPS1. Measured node optimum is 8 cores, one CCX. Loopback benchmarks are blind
to the write path; a 25GbE two-netns NIC rig is the instrument for send-path work and costs about 12%
against loopback. Box noise is ±0.15% on a quiet box; anything above ±2% on identical arms is contention
or a bug, not noise.

**The gate boots nothing like a default server.** `tests/gate.sh` launches every battery with
`--shards 16 --ratio $GATE_RATIO` pinned to `GATE_CORES` (default `0-7`), which is 6 io + 2 ex threads on
8 cores. Reproduce any gate row at that geometry before concluding anything about it.

## What it is measured against

Redis 7.4 and 8.8.1, Dragonfly 1.40.2, KeyDB, Microsoft Garnet (net10.0), memcached 1.6.45, plus YCSB
0.17.0 traces. Binaries and digests: `/home/user/Projects/bench-bins/MANIFEST.md`.

We do not win everywhere and the paper will not claim we do. At 64 real cores and pipeline depth 128,
Garnet reaches 62.8M ops/s against our 34.4M. We hold depth 1, where we reach 4.35M. Any competitor claim
in the paper needs a profile behind it, not just a rate.

## How performance is judged

**cycles/op = instructions/op ÷ IPC.** Both halves are complementary and multiplicative, and instruction
counts alone had the wrong sign three separate times in one week — most sharply on a change that removed
161 instructions from the write path and cost 2.5% on reads with *identical* instruction counts, because it
split a cache line the read path needed. Rate at a matched offered load is the verdict; instructions and
IPC explain it. Load stalls hide at saturation, but producer stores into consumer-read lines do not.

Every optimization lands with a PRE vs POST table. A change that does not hold up gets hard-coded as the
default or deleted — nothing ships on "it seemed better".

## Why this work looks the way it does

Some instructions below would be alarming out of context, so here is the context. This is a single-user
research box. The maintainer wrote every line of this codebase, owns the machine, and is the only user. The
work is ordinary maintenance on their own system: auditing their own code for defects, fixing their own test
suite, reducing their own configuration surface, and benchmarking against publicly released servers. Nothing
here touches anyone else's data, systems or accounts.

Four specifics that read oddly without the reason:

1. **"Never run the server, the benchmark or the gate."** This is about measurement integrity and nothing
   else. Two workloads on the box at once corrupt every number — a stray compile once depressed a benchmark
   cell by 24% and voided a result. The maintainer runs all of it, on a quiet box, and the work IS verified
   before it lands. You are being asked to produce a diff, not to skip verification.

2. **"Never edit `EXPECT_QUICK` / `EXPECT_FULL`."** Those constants are how many test rows must pass. Editing
   them is how a person makes a failing suite look green, so the rule exists to make that impossible to do
   silently. It is a stricter standard than normal, not a looser one. State what the count should become and
   why; the maintainer changes it.

3. **Concurrency vocabulary.** This is a database. "Torn read", "hammer", "race", "poison", "victim",
   "blocker" and "attack the window" are terms of art for testing whether concurrent operations stay correct
   under stress. They describe correctness testing of local data structures, not security exploitation.

4. **Deliberately breaking a mechanism to check a test.** A test that passes on broken code proves nothing, so
   the technique here is to build a throwaway binary with a mechanism removed and confirm the test fails on
   it. That build is never committed and never runs outside the box. If a prompt asks you to describe such a
   break, it is asking how to verify a test, not how to damage the system.

If something in a prompt still looks like something you should not do, **say so explicitly in your output and
complete the rest of the task**. A stated objection is useful. Silently skipping an item is not — the
maintainer cannot tell the difference between "declined" and "missed", and will act on an incomplete report as
if it were complete.

## Working rules for codex

- **Never run a server, a benchmark, or the gate.** The maintainer runs the box. Report, or produce a diff.
- Edit only inside your own worktree.
- Never edit `EXPECT_QUICK` / `EXPECT_FULL` in `tests/gate.sh`. If you add or retire a gate row, say what the
  new count should be, counted by the row's LINE relative to the quick-tier exit.
- Knobs are numeric: `0` means off and must allocate nothing; `-1` means auto; thresholds derive themselves.
  Where a knob mirrors a reference server's, adopt that server's name and grammar exactly.
- A test that cannot fail proves nothing. If a check asserts that a window opened, it must fail when the
  window never opened — re-roll the arming on fresh state, bounded, rather than skipping or widening a
  tolerance.

## Closed doors — measured, negative, do not re-propose

`3s` three-stage mode; `exwb` executor-side writeback (−11 to −22%); AMAC and any CR/MR split (the only
boundary is io/ex); reorder-and-window; seqlocks on the per-op path; connection-side record allocation
(`connalloc`, cycles flat, record born on the wrong core); executor-major task collapse (`exmajor`,
−2 to −3%); the read-local capacity hand-off line split (`t-pubdiet`, +1.97% SET but −2.50% GET).

#!/bin/bash
# PRE-PUSH GATE for tomokv-cpp (pure 2s baseline).
#
#   tests/gate.sh quick   loopback only: build (release+ASAN), footprint locks, boot
#                         matrix, smoke, torture, RYOW, atomic torn/mixed-write/window gates,
#                         shutdown invariants, counter-fired assertions, idle-loop ceiling. Runs on
#                         any machine.
#   tests/gate.sh full    quick + torture-under-ASAN + the Redis 7.4 differential matrix + NIC
#                         regression cells vs tests/gate_refs.txt (the NIC cells need the 25GbE
#                         netns rig and its scratchpad binaries/procsafe helper).
#
#   Every feature battery runs on three boots: split (both atomic modes), fused, and fused with the
#   read-local lane ARMED (--read-local 1, the recommended read-heavy production posture; that leg
#   is the only one on which a clean GET/MGET is served by the lane instead of an owner).
#
#   GATE_QUIET_FILE=<path> (opt-in, for a shared box): nothing that starts CPU work -- a battery, a
#   boot, a build, a load generator -- is launched unless that file exists and is older than
#   GATE_QUIET_MINUTES (3). A running battery always finishes; a build is SIGSTOPped; the idle server
#   is SIGSTOPped while waiting; waited time is taken out of the ledger's per-row seconds and logged
#   to $LEDGER.pauses. GATE_LEDGER overrides the ledger path.
#
# The vacuous-validation rule is load-bearing here: every section proves its mechanism FIRED
# (counters, accepts, direct>0), not merely that nothing crashed. A gate that can pass while
# testing nothing is worse than no gate.
set -u
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
TIER=${1:-quick}
PORT=${GATE_PORT:-7899}
CORES=${GATE_CORES:-0-7}
NCORES=$(taskset -c "$CORES" nproc)
if [ "$NCORES" -ge 8 ]; then GATE_RATIO=6:$((NCORES-6))
else GATE_RATIO=$(((NCORES+1)/2)):$((NCORES-(NCORES+1)/2)); fi
PASS=0; FAIL=0
SRV=0; SRVLOG=/dev/null
GLOBCASE_ORACLE=0; MMPID=0
# The pinned vanilla Redis 7.4 tree (source + built src/redis-server). The ACL-category generator
# reads its SOURCE in both tiers; the differential and globcase rows boot its BINARY in the full
# tier. The preflight below says exactly what is missing instead of a traceback in row 4.
export REDIS74_ROOT=${REDIS74_ROOT:-/tmp/claude-1000/redis74}
# Wall-time bound per battery (see py()). A hung battery used to hang the whole gate; now it is a
# red row that says TIMEOUT. 900 s is ~3x the slowest battery on the gate cores. flipctl.py is
# launched with its own explicit 600 s bound (it re-rolls a non-stationary stable hold; see there).
GATE_TEST_TIMEOUT=${GATE_TEST_TIMEOUT:-900}
# A battery that records a STRICT skip (a DEBUG hook it needed was denied) fails under the gate:
# a gate row must run the arm it exists for, never turn green by skipping it (tests/_lib.py).
export TOMO_GATE_STRICT=1
# Machine-readable ledger, one line per row: verdict, seconds since the previous row, label.
# It is the runtime-distribution instrument (which rows own the 45 minutes) and, when the count
# drifts, the diff against the previous run's ledger names the row that vanished or appeared.
LEDGER=${GATE_LEDGER:-/tmp/gate-ledger-$TIER.txt}
[ -f "$LEDGER" ] && mv -f "$LEDGER" "$LEDGER.prev"
: > "$LEDGER"
ROW_T=$(date +%s.%N)
# Expected check counts. These are the whole point of the ledger row: a battery that silently
# stops running drops the count and turns the gate red instead of quietly shrinking coverage.
# Bump them DELIBERATELY when rows are added, and say which rows in the commit message.
# 152 -> 172: the s6 oracle battery, concur, execiso and xacct, each under both atomic modes.
# 172 -> 178: snapcut added two cross-shard snapshot-cut rows per persist-io engine, and execfix
# added its battery under both atomic modes.
# 178 -> 184: edgeproto, edgeenc and edgetime batteries joined the feature loop (both modes each).
# 184 -> 189: cross-owner scripts add their battery under both atomic modes plus three control
# boots (off / byte-limit / window), each needing its own knob value and so its own server.
# 189 -> 192: the three efficiency guards, each on its own boot geometry.
# 192 -> 194: the AOF frame-order battery, on persist-io normal under both atomic modes.
# 194 -> 207: arity, blockmulti, cmdgap, multires and xmove were shipped but not invoked; aclsel,
# cmdmeta and expwide joined the feature loop; cmdmeta coverage is a new static row. Each feature

# 207 -> 211: contarity exercises XGROUP/XINFO under the feature boot's 16-shard, >=2-executor

# 211 -> 213: cross-owner SORT has its required 16-shard, 6:2 geometry under both atomic modes.
# 213 -> 215: pushtear proves out-of-band frames cannot splice borrowed replies and requires the
# segmented/deferred and zero-copy counters to fire, under both atomic modes.
# 215 -> 224: nine rows landed without a history line (two sibling lanes each claimed 207 -> 209

# 224 -> 236: fused mode adds one boot-line assertion plus five directed batteries (s6,

# 236 -> 238: atomic MGET/MSET throughput floor + tripwire arm/disarm round-trip (a 9x armed-by-
# default tax on the atomic chain read once passed this gate with nothing measuring the path).
# 238 -> 239: pipelined same-connection program order (seed-19 divergence; 74% stale pre-fix).
# 239 -> 240: the flip-controller model unit test (tests/flipctl_unit.cc) as a static build row;
# it compiled clean but nothing built or ran it (AUDIT-TESTS F15). Full: 250 -> 251.
# 240 -> 241: atomic_hazards locks the S1 FLUSH read-cut and S2 XREAD touched-key fixes on the

# 241 -> 243: B+ adds the counting-fingerprint representation unit plus the deterministic

# 243 -> 245 quick: each fused boot now proves its schema-1 final report is present, clean, and
# labels itself as fused instead of relying only on the live INFO assertion. Full: 254 -> 256.
# 256 -> 258 full: the CLIENT REPLY OFF/SKIP cross-shard MGET zero-copy rows (both atomic modes).
# 245 -> 246 quick, 258 -> 259 full: the armed local-read lane-admission battery on the B+ boot

# deltas to the shared base rather than by taking one side: 245+2 / 258+2+3 = 247/263.
# Merged: 322 quick + 2 (multirace: the multi_exec order-late row per atomic mode) = 324;
# 335 full + 3 = 338. Additions are disjoint from the fused+armed and lane-admission rows.
# 258 -> 260 full: reply codes make a blocking timeout's "*-1"/"_" a CODE rather than bytes, so the

# Merged: the aclreply battery adds one row per thread mode and both run BEFORE the quick-tier exit,

# 340 -> 343 full: the armed-write block cache's ownership laws (DESIGN-P0REPLY.md). A shard that

# thread's unlocked free list. Three rows: the -DTOMO_RL_CACHE_DEBUG build, the churn battery on it
# (which carries its own non-vacuity checks, including that the balancer MOVED shards), and the
# invariant check over that server's log.
# COUNTED BY LINE, NOT BY INFERENCE (which is what produced the 324/326 correction above): the
# quick tier exits at the `[ "$TIER" = quick ]` block, and all three rows are emitted after it, so
# they are full-only. Quick is unchanged at 326; full is 340 + 3 = 343.
# 324 -> 325 quick (340 -> 341 full): the RYOW write-ring unit joins the static rows, carrying the
# arm-on-demand transient cases (t-ringdiet, DESIGN-RINGDIET.md). One row in BOTH tiers, because it
# is server-less and costs under two seconds; the arithmetic is 324+1 / 340+1 and it is disjoint

# Merged 2026-09-07: the ring unit is one row in BOTH tiers (server-less, under two seconds), so

EXPECT_QUICK=325
EXPECT_FULL=342                 # full without the optional NIC row.
say(){ printf '  %-52s %s\n' "$1" "$2"; }
ledger(){ # verdict label -> one ledger line; the elapsed column is wall time since the last row
  local now; now=$(date +%s.%N)
  printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$1" "$(awk -v a="$ROW_T" -v b="$now" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1f", b-a}')" "$2" \
      >> "$LEDGER"
  ROW_T=$now
}
ok(){ say "$1" "ok"; PASS=$((PASS+1)); ledger ok "$1"; }
bad(){ say "$1" "FAIL${2:+ ($2)}"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); ledger FAIL "$1"; }
ledger_labels(){ cut -f3 "$1" | sed 's/[0-9][0-9]*/N/g' | sort; }
program_state(){
  local expect=$1 actual=$((PASS+FAIL))
  if [ "$actual" -eq "$expect" ]; then
    say "PROGRAM-STATE ledger ($actual/$expect checks)" "ok"
  else
    bad "PROGRAM-STATE ledger" "$actual/$expect checks"
    if [ -f "$LEDGER.prev" ]; then
      echo "  rows that differ from the previous $TIER ledger (< only in previous run, > only now):"
      diff <(ledger_labels "$LEDGER.prev") <(ledger_labels "$LEDGER") | grep '^[<>]' | sed 's/^/    /'
    fi
  fi
  echo "  ledger: $LEDGER (verdict / seconds since previous row / label); slowest rows:"
  sort -t "$(printf '\t')" -k2,2 -rn "$LEDGER" | head -12 \
      | awk -F '\t' '{printf "    %7.1fs  %-4s %s\n", $2, $1, $3}'
}
redis_cli_expect_ok(){
  local reply
  reply=$(redis-cli -h 127.0.0.1 -p "$PORT" "$@" 2>&1 | tr -d '\r')
  [ "$reply" = OK ] || { printf 'unexpected redis-cli reply to %s: %s\n' "$*" "$reply" >&2; return 1; }
}
# Cooperative box sharing (opt-in, see header). quiet_ok is the whole rule; its two callers are
# quiet_wait (before anything that starts CPU work) and pausable (around a build -- the one kind
# of row long enough to need stopping mid-flight and free of timing semantics).
QUIET_FILE=${GATE_QUIET_FILE:-}
QUIET_MIN=${GATE_QUIET_MINUTES:-3}
PAUSABLE_PID=0
quiet_ok(){ [ -z "$QUIET_FILE" ] || [ -n "$(find "$QUIET_FILE" -mmin +"$QUIET_MIN" 2>/dev/null)" ]; }
quiet_note(){ printf '%s %s\n' "$(date '+%H:%M:%S')" "$*" | tee -a "$LEDGER.pauses" >&2; }
quiet_wait(){ # block until quiet_ok. The live server is SIGSTOPped meanwhile (an idle fused loop
              # still spins on cores an owner measurement may share); the waited time leaves the
              # ledger's next row, which measures rows, not the box.
  quiet_ok && return 0
  local t0 now stopped=0
  t0=$(date +%s.%N)
  if [ "$SRV" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null && kill -0 "$SRV" 2>/dev/null; then
    kill -STOP "$SRV" 2>/dev/null && stopped=1
  fi
  quiet_note "quiet: waiting for $QUIET_FILE to be >$QUIET_MIN min old" \
      "($([ "$stopped" = 1 ] && echo "server $SRV stopped" || echo "no server up"))"
  until quiet_ok; do sleep 5; done
  [ "$stopped" = 1 ] && kill -CONT "$SRV" 2>/dev/null
  now=$(date +%s.%N)
  ROW_T=$(awk -v a="$ROW_T" -v b="$t0" -v c="$now" 'BEGIN{printf "%.9f", a + (c - b)}')
  quiet_note "quiet: resumed after $(awk -v b="$t0" -v c="$now" 'BEGIN{printf "%.0f", c - b}')s"
}
pausable(){ # run "$@" to completion (its exit status is ours); SIGSTOP its whole process group
            # whenever quiet_ok turns false and SIGCONT it when the file is back. Builds only.
  [ -n "$QUIET_FILE" ] || { "$@"; return $?; }
  quiet_wait
  local pid stopped=0 t0=0 paused=0 rc
  setsid "$@" &
  pid=$!; PAUSABLE_PID=$pid
  while kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; do
    if quiet_ok; then
      if [ "$stopped" = 1 ]; then
        kill -CONT -- "-$pid" 2>/dev/null; stopped=0
        paused=$(awk -v p="$paused" -v b="$t0" -v c="$(date +%s.%N)" \
                     'BEGIN{printf "%.3f", p + (c - b)}')
        quiet_note "quiet: build resumed"
      fi
    elif [ "$stopped" = 0 ]; then
      kill -STOP -- "-$pid" 2>/dev/null; stopped=1; t0=$(date +%s.%N)
      quiet_note "quiet: build paused until $QUIET_FILE is >$QUIET_MIN min old"
    fi
    sleep 2
  done
  wait "$pid"; rc=$?
  PAUSABLE_PID=0
  ROW_T=$(awk -v a="$ROW_T" -v p="$paused" 'BEGIN{printf "%.9f", a + p}')
  return $rc
}
py(){ # python3 battery wrapper: bounded wall time. A timeout or a self-skip (exit 3, see
      # tests/_lib.skip_all) is named in the row's log (callers redirect our stderr there) and
      # stays RED: a row that cannot run is a gate defect, not a pass. --foreground keeps the
      # battery in the terminal's process group so Ctrl-C reaches it too.
  local rc
  quiet_wait
  timeout --foreground "$GATE_TEST_TIMEOUT" python3 "$@"; rc=$?
  case $rc in
    124) echo "GATE: TIMEOUT -- battery killed after ${GATE_TEST_TIMEOUT}s" >&2;;
    3)   echo "GATE: battery SKIPPED ITSELF (exit 3): a gate row must run, not skip" >&2;;
  esac
  return $rc
}
cleanup(){ # EXIT/INT/TERM: never leave the server on $PORT, the globcase oracle, or memtier behind
  local p
  if [ "$PAUSABLE_PID" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then   # a build parked by pausable
    kill -CONT -- "-$PAUSABLE_PID" 2>/dev/null; kill -TERM -- "-$PAUSABLE_PID" 2>/dev/null

# Findings that survived adversarial review

Each was attacked by a skeptic instructed to refute it and could not be killed.
MISPRICED means true but wrongly ranked -- fix it, but weight it by its real reachability.

1. **S storage 13 — MISPRICED: deadline-sidecar expiry.**  
   The ordinary build reads the object’s inline deadline. The stale-index deadline becomes authoritative only with `TOMO_TTL_DEADLINE_SIDECAR=1`, whose default is zero. The prototype failure remains credible: extend a deadline while the index needs allocation, fail that allocation, then read after the previous deadline. Classify this as a prototype-build defect requiring allocation failure. [Selector](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/store_ttl.h:8), [deadline accessor](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore.h:1454).

2. **C concurrency 2 — MISPRICED: scheduler stack bounds.**  
   The stated `--overlap` and `--ex-sched` flags are rejected. However, their accepted replacements, `--x-overlap 1 --x-ex-sched 1`, still expose the mismatch in fused mode. A gathered batch containing at least 33 eligible commands reaches the 32-entry array before the single-client shortcut. This is a real memory-safety defect in an explicitly enabled experimental combination; it does not describe the default scheduler configuration. [Parser](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/config.h:632), [scheduler](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/ex_loop.h:2303).

3. **S cmdsem F08 — MISPRICED: failed/no-op writes dirty WATCH.**  
   The unconditional write-completion hook does dirty the declared key after `WRONGTYPE` or an unsuccessful `SET NX`. The supplied sequence therefore produces a spurious EXEC abort. The traced failure is pessimistic conflict detection: it does not admit a transaction that should fail or commit an incorrect value. Retain a compatibility/progress finding at reduced severity. [Completion hook](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/ex_loop.h:2967), [dirtying](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/multi.inc:2413).

4. **S deadconf F08 — MISPRICED: statistics races.**  
   RESETSTAT captures a baseline; it does not zero foreign owner counters. That substantially limits the allegation. Nevertheless, capture still reads plain counters concurrently, and an atomic load does not make a concurrent plain store race-free. Retain the C++ race and measurement-validity defect; keyspace corruption or process failure is not established by this claim. [Counter reads](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_server.cc:1584), [RESETSTAT](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_server.cc:2940), [LB reader](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/lbsignals.cc:14).

5. **S atomics 15 — MISPRICED: shared staging-failure flag.**  
   Two owner tasks can both pass the initial abort check, independently exceed the staging cap, and race while storing `script_stage_limit=true`. The atomic byte total does not order those plain stores. However, each task separately records an error and publishes atomic abort state; the demonstrated defect is an error-path data race, without an established incorrect commit. No removed tuning knob is needed: with maxmemory off, two owner images exceeding the derived 4 MiB cap suffice. [Stores](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/scatter_engine.inc:2444), [derived cap](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/server.h:253).

6. **S cmdsem F15 — MISPRICED: runtime string-size limit.**  
   The mismatch is real: after setting the limit to 1 MiB, `SETRANGE k 1048576 x` passes the private 512 MiB bound. Its scope is a nondefault configuration inconsistency; it does not bypass the independent maxmemory mechanism, and growth remains bounded by the private constant. Retain as a limit-enforcement compatibility defect at reduced severity. [String bound](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_string.cc:60), [bitmap bound](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/bitfield.inc:8).

8. **C atomics 1; C storage 1 — SURVIVES: admission evicts an unlinked candidate.**  
   I checked both victim exclusions. Neither sees an earlier candidate belonging only to the currently unlinked group. With atomic scatter, positive maxmemory, an allkeys policy, read-local disabled and no borrow, admit/install fresh `a`, then make admission of same-shard `b` select `a`. Erase frees it before group publication, while `stable_object` retains its address. A third key on another owner supplies the scatter trigger. [Install ordering](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/scatter_engine.inc:2775), [admission exclusions](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore_atomic.inc:443).

9. **C atomics 2 — SURVIVES: retained registration closure.**  
   Restoring the global `redis` table does not revoke a closure retained by a registered callback. Load the supplied library that saves `redis.register_function`, then invoke its callback through FCALL. Materialization has returned before that callback reuses the closure’s pointer to its stack-local `RegisterSink`. The non-null check does not establish lifetime. Actual crash behavior depends on stack reuse; the invalid lifetime access does not. [Closure creation](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/functions.cc:434), [materialization lifetime](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/functions.cc:581).

    EVAL’s CursorShard classification routes execution using its actual declared keys, but transaction `write_keys` still includes ARGV through generic metadata. Promotion cannot remove that protected version, and same-connection ordering guards do not apply between A and B. The two replies can both be 1.     The speculative geometry can be made concrete. Start with 700 live keys in a 1,024-slot table. A cross-owner atomic DEL removing those 700 keys preflights a 2,048-slot destination. Delay its other fragment before failure. After local deletion, insert 1,400 unrelated keys, choosing them to reuse tombstones before empty slots; this remains below the ordinary 70% growth threshold. Now fail the delayed fragment and let cleanup allocations succeed. Restoring 700 distinct predecessors requires 2,100 live slots in capacity 2,048.

1. **S storage 13 — MISPRICED: deadline-sidecar expiry.**  
   The ordinary build reads the object’s inline deadline. The stale-index deadline becomes authoritative only with `TOMO_TTL_DEADLINE_SIDECAR=1`, whose default is zero. The prototype failure remains credible: extend a deadline while the index needs allocation, fail that allocation, then read after the previous deadline. Classify this as a prototype-build defect requiring allocation failure. [Selector](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/store_ttl.h:8), [deadline accessor](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore.h:1454).

2. **C concurrency 2 — MISPRICED: scheduler stack bounds.**  
   The stated `--overlap` and `--ex-sched` flags are rejected. However, their accepted replacements, `--x-overlap 1 --x-ex-sched 1`, still expose the mismatch in fused mode. A gathered batch containing at least 33 eligible commands reaches the 32-entry array before the single-client shortcut. B’s eventual rename failure does not undo that write. The config mutex protects only snapshot collection. Protected mode may restrict connection origins, but it does not restore the specified password. CXX      ?= g++
JEDIR    ?= /home/user/Projects/refs/jemalloc/_install
# jemalloc is optional: without it the tree still builds and runs, using the deterministic portable
# size-class table in alloc.h. Set JE=0 to force that path (useful for A/B-ing the allocator).
JE       ?= 1
ifeq ($(JE),1)
  # Prefer the system package; fall back to the copy built from refs/.
  ifneq ($(wildcard /usr/include/jemalloc/jemalloc.h),)
    JEFLAGS := -DTOMO_JEMALLOC
    JELIBS  := -ljemalloc
  else
    JEFLAGS := -DTOMO_JEMALLOC -I$(JEDIR)/include
    JELIBS  := $(JEDIR)/lib/libjemalloc.a -ldl
  endif
else
  JEFLAGS :=
  JELIBS  :=
endif
CXXFLAGS ?= -std=c++20 -O2 -g -Wall -Wextra -march=native -pthread
LDLIBS   ?= -luring -pthread
SRC      := src/main.cc src/net/tls.cc src/cmd/commands.cc src/cmd/glob.cc src/cmd/xshard.cc src/cmd/acl.cc src/cmd/hll.cc src/cmd/t_server.cc src/cmd/t_string.cc src/cmd/t_string_notify.cc src/cmd/t_hash.cc src/cmd/t_hash_ttl.cc \
            src/cmd/t_list.cc src/cmd/t_set.cc src/cmd/t_zset.cc src/cmd/t_zset_ops.cc src/cmd/geo.cc src/cmd/t_stream.cc src/cmd/t_stream_groups.cc src/cmd/scripting.cc src/cmd/functions.cc src/cmd/serialize.cc src/snapshot/snapshot.cc src/persist/aof.cc
SRC      += src/cmd/climon.cc src/cmd/tracking.cc

SRC      += src/cmd/lbsignals.cc
SRC      += src/core/flipctl.cc
SRC      += src/core/genthread.cc
SRC      += src/cmd/cmdgap.cc
SRC      += src/cmd/pfdebug.cc
SRC      += src/cmd/cmdmeta.cc
SRC      += src/cmd/t_sort.cc
LDLIBS   += -lssl -lcrypto
BIN      := build/tomokv
OBJ      := $(SRC:%.cc=build/%.o)

all: $(BIN)

$(BIN): $(OBJ)
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) $(OBJ) -o $@ $(JELIBS) $(LDLIBS) -lm

# The clean string family intentionally excludes the armed instantiations, but its parsed template

# decisions as the base-420b4d492 translation unit; the objdump gate locks cmd_get/cmd_set to base.
build/src/cmd/t_string.o: CXXFLAGS += --param large-unit-insns=10600

build/%.o: %.cc $(wildcard src/*/*.h) $(wildcard src/*/*.inc) $(wildcard third_party/lua/*) Makefile

asan:

tsan:
	@mkdir -p build
	$(CXX) -std=c++20 -O1 -g -Wall -Wextra -pthread -fsanitize=thread \
	  -I. $(SRC) -o build/tomokv-tsan $(LDLIBS) -lm

# The armed-write block cache's ownership laws as assertions: the cache and the QSBR retire ring
# are owner-private (one thread, no lock), each cached block is resident exactly once, each class
# list matches its counter, and every shard's retire sink names its CURRENT owner. Debug-only: the
# residency set and the sampled list walk cost far more than the path they guard. DESIGN-P0REPLY.md.
rlcachedbg:
	@mkdir -p build
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) $(JEFLAGS) -DTOMO_RL_CACHE_DEBUG -I. $(SRC) \
	  -o build/tomokv-rlcachedbg $(JELIBS) $(LDLIBS) -lm

# NEGATIVE-CONTROL BUILD for the row above: the same assertions with the ownership-edge rebind
# removed, i.e. the pre-fix behaviour. tests/rlcache_churn.py MUST fail against this binary; a
# detector that cannot report failure proves nothing about the runs that pass.
rlcache-nofix:

	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) $(JEFLAGS) -DTOMO_RL_CACHE_DEBUG -DTOMO_RL_CACHE_NO_EAGER_ADOPT -I. $(SRC) \
	  -o build/tomokv-rlcache-nofix $(JELIBS) $(LDLIBS) -lm

# NEGATIVE-CONTROL BUILD for the cross-owner script reservation sub-wave. Identical to the release
# build except that ScriptPhase::Pin arms nothing, so tests/xscript.py counterexample MUST fail
# against it. A detector that cannot report failure proves nothing about the runs that pass.
noreserve:
	@mkdir -p build
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) $(JEFLAGS) -DTOMO_XSCRIPT_NO_RESERVE -I. $(SRC) \
	  -o build/tomokv-noreserve $(JELIBS) $(LDLIBS) -lm

	@mkdir -p build

build/read-local-ring-unit: tests/read_local_ring_unit.cc $(wildcard src/*/*.h) Makefile
	@mkdir -p build

build/read-local-write-ring-unit: tests/read_local_write_ring_unit.cc $(wildcard src/*/*.h) Makefile

unit: build/config-parser-test build/flipctl-unit build/read-local-ring-unit build/read-local-write-ring-unit

	./build/read-local-ring-unit
	./build/read-local-write-ring-unit

build/benchtxn: tools/benchtxn.cc Makefile
	@mkdir -p build
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) -I. tools/benchtxn.cc -o $@

	@mkdir -p build

tools: build/benchtxn build/broaden-bench

clean:
	rm -rf build

// multi.inc -- MULTI/EXEC/DISCARD/WATCH/UNWATCH on the epoch-MVCC seam.
//
// This file is textually included by xshard.cc.  It shares the command-image helpers in the same
// anonymous namespace and deliberately creates no extra translation unit.

namespace tomo {

struct MultiQueuedCommand {
    const CommandSpec* spec = nullptr;
    std::vector<std::string> argv;
};

struct MultiWatchedKey {
    std::string key;
    uint64_t hash = 0;
    int32_t shard = -1;
};

enum class MultiCommandKind : uint8_t {
    Local,
    Mget,
    Mset,
    Msetnx,
    Del,
    Exists,
    Ping,
    Echo,
    UnwatchReply,
    IoLocal,
    Scan,
    Xshard,
    Prebuilt,
    Unsupported,
};

enum class MultiBlockingPop : uint8_t {
    None, Blpop, Brpop, Blmpop, Bzpopmin, Bzpopmax, Bzmpop
};

struct MultiValue {
    bool present = false;
    std::string value;
};

struct MultiCommand {
    static constexpr uint32_t kXshardStages = 4;
    static constexpr uint32_t kShardMaskWords = 4;

    MultiQueuedCommand queued;
    std::unique_ptr<Op> op;
    MultiCommandKind kind = MultiCommandKind::Unsupported;
    std::vector<uint32_t> key_args;
    std::vector<int32_t> key_shards;
    std::vector<int32_t> participants;
    std::vector<uint8_t> shard_done;
    std::vector<MultiValue> values;
    // Blocking collection commands are executed inside EXEC through a nonblocking LMPOP/ZMPOP
    // child. The normalized argv owns the slices installed in `op`; it allocates only for these
    // transaction-only slow-path commands.
    std::vector<std::string> exec_argv;
    MultiBlockingPop blocking_pop = MultiBlockingPop::None;
    uint8_t pop_reply_shape = static_cast<uint8_t>(PopReplyShape::Mpop);
    std::atomic<uint32_t> pending{0};
    std::atomic<uint32_t> stage{0};
    std::atomic<long long> integer{0};
    std::atomic<bool> condition_failed{false};
    std::atomic<bool> finished{false};
    ScatterState* scatter = nullptr;
    // ScatterState::groups is rebuilt between an xshard child's waves.  A barrier-only shard must
    // decide whether it belongs to the PUBLISHED wave without consulting that mutable table: the
    // last task from the prior wave is allowed to rewrite it before publishing command.stage.
    // Four 64-bit words cover the server's 256-shard maximum.  Four stages cover the longest child
    // today (SORT source -> dynamic gather -> STORE apply) with one spare stage for a future retry.
    std::array<std::array<uint64_t, kShardMaskWords>, kXshardStages> xshard_stage_groups{};
    uint32_t notify_order_base = 0;
};

enum class MultiStateKind : uint8_t { Execute, WatchAdd, Unwatch, Close };
enum class MultiFinalReply : uint8_t { Exec, Ok, ExecAbort };

struct MultiWriteKey {
    std::string key;
    uint64_t hash = 0;
    int32_t shard = -1;
};

struct MultiWriteKeyHash {
    size_t operator()(const MultiWriteKey& key) const {
        return static_cast<size_t>(key.hash ^
            (static_cast<uint64_t>(static_cast<uint32_t>(key.shard)) *
             0x9e3779b97f4a7c15ULL));
    }
};

struct MultiWriteKeyEqual {
    bool operator()(const MultiWriteKey& left, const MultiWriteKey& right) const {
        return left.shard == right.shard && left.key == right.key;
    }
};

struct MultiSession {
    bool active = false;
    bool queue_error = false;
    uint64_t next_queue_op_id = 0;
    std::vector<MultiQueuedCommand> queue;
    std::vector<MultiWatchedKey> watched;
    MultiExecState* pending = nullptr;       // prepared, but not yet published to owner queues
};

struct MultiOwnerRecordRefs {
    // `nodes` is also the pointer retained by every AtomicEntry installed on this executor. Writer
    // owners begin at one so cleanup cannot release the state's pre-count before the owner has run
    // all of its outer shard tasks through the transaction's final decision.
    uint32_t nodes = 0;
    uint32_t remaining = 0;
    bool completion_sentinel = false;
};

// EXEC MUST NEVER BE WEAKER THAN THE SAME COMMANDS RUN BARE.  A bare cross-shard read pins a read
// cut, so a transaction that carries one has to pin a cut too; SnapshotCut is the shared header
// that lets it do so through the connection-owning IO thread's ScatterArenaPool, which is the one
// object allowed to write that thread's published cleanup floor (see xshard.h).
struct alignas(8) MultiExecState : SnapshotCut {
    ~MultiExecState() { notify_discard_batch(notify.exchange(nullptr)); }
    MultiStateKind kind = MultiStateKind::Execute;
    MultiFinalReply final_reply = MultiFinalReply::Exec;
    Server* server = nullptr;
    Client* client = nullptr;
    uint32_t owner_io = 0;
    uint64_t origin_conn_id = 0;
    uint64_t watch_generation = 0;
    uint64_t admission_generation = 0;
    bool admitted = false;
    bool reset_watch = false;
    bool published = false;
    bool retired = false;
    // Set at prepare time when the transaction carries at least one READ whose fragments land on
    // more than one owner -- the only shape that can straddle a foreign ticket, and therefore the
    // only shape that pays for a cut.  A write-only or single-owner transaction registers nothing.
    bool exec_read_fanout = false;
    // THE TRANSACTION'S EXPIRY CUT, the time-axis twin of the read cut above.  Absolute
    // CLOCK_REALTIME milliseconds, stamped once before any fragment is posted and installed on
    // every owner that runs part of this transaction.  Redis reaches the same place from the other
    // direction: EXEC is the top-level call, the queued commands run nested inside it, and

    std::vector<std::vector<uint32_t>> shard_commands;
    std::vector<uint32_t> shard_cursors;
    std::vector<uint8_t> watch_shard_done;
    std::vector<uint8_t> execution_joined;
    std::vector<uint8_t> final_shard_done;

    std::vector<uint8_t> execution_noted;

    std::atomic<uint32_t> record_refs{0};

    std::atomic<bool> watch_failed{false};
    std::atomic<bool> watch_phase_done{false};
    std::atomic<uint32_t> watch_pending{0};
    std::atomic<uint32_t> lists_pending{0};
    std::atomic<bool> finalizer_claimed{false};

constexpr uintptr_t kMultiTaskTag = 1;

bool multi_name(const Op& op, const char* lower) { return op.cmd_name().eq_icase(lower); }

MultiSession* ensure_multi_session(Client& client) {
    if (client.multi_session()) return client.multi_session();
    auto* session = new (std::nothrow) MultiSession;
    if (session) client.set_multi_session(session);
    return session;
}

void release_admission(MultiExecState& state) {
    if (state.server)
        state.server->atomic_apply_close(state.owner_io, state.apply_open);
    if (!state.admitted) return;
    state.server->atomic_retire_group(state.owner_io, state.admission_generation);
    state.admitted = false;
}

// Does `group_epoch` name a word THIS transaction publishes through? A transaction is one logical
// unit spread over several epoch words: the plain per-key installs publish through `state.epoch`,
// and every cross-shard command lowered inside the same EXEC keeps its own ScatterState and
// publishes through that one. Anything asking "is there an undecided record here that is not mine"
// has to accept all of them, or the transaction answers yes against its own RENAME/LMPOP child.
// `commands` and their scatter pointers are written by IO in prepare_commands() before the first
// fragment is posted, and cleared only by destroy_multi_children() at retirement, which cannot run
// while a fragment is still executing -- so this walk is stable on an owner thread.
bool multi_state_owns_epoch(const MultiExecState& state, const void* group_epoch) {
    if (!group_epoch) return false;
    if (group_epoch == static_cast<const void*>(&state.epoch)) return true;
    for (const auto& command : state.commands)
        if (command && command->scatter &&
            group_epoch == static_cast<const void*>(&command->scatter->epoch))
            return true;
    return false;
}

bool multi_records_done(const MultiExecState& state) {
    if (state.record_refs.load(std::memory_order_acquire) != 0 ||
        state.watch_refs.load(std::memory_order_acquire) != 0) return false;
    for (const auto& command : state.commands)
        if (command->scatter && !xshard_multi_child_records_done(*command->scatter)) return false;
    return true;
}

void destroy_multi_children(MultiExecState& state) {
    for (const auto& command : state.commands) {
        if (!command->scatter) continue;
        xshard_destroy(command->scatter, state.scatter_pool, state.owner_io);
        command->scatter = nullptr;
    }
    state.scatter_pool.reap_deferred();
}

void destroy_multi_state(MultiExecState* state) {
    if (!state) return;
    if (__builtin_expect(atomic_tripwire_enabled(), false))
        atomic_tripwire_forget_scope(state);
    if (!multi_records_done(*state)) std::abort();
    // The cut bracket is register-at-dispatch / unregister-at-retire, both on the connection's own
    // IO thread. Reaching destruction still holding it would mean this thread's published cleanup
    // floor is pinned to a dead transaction, so cleanup would stop advancing server-wide. That is
    // an engine invariant, not an input condition; make it loud rather than silently degrading.
    if (state->snapshot_registered) std::abort();
    destroy_multi_children(*state);
    release_admission(*state);
    delete state;
}

bool command_forbidden_in_multi(const Op& op) {
    // Subscription controls need the IO-owned async home protocol, which cannot run from an EXEC
    // child. Reject all six controls uniformly; this is intentionally stricter than Redis for the
    // four regular controls and matches it for SSUBSCRIBE/SUNSUBSCRIBE.
    const bool config_mutation = multi_name(op, "config") && op.argc() > 1 &&
                                 !op.arg(1).eq_icase("get");
    return (op.spec->flags & CmdFlags::NoMulti) ||
           multi_name(op, "save") || multi_name(op, "flushall") ||
           multi_name(op, "flushdb") || config_mutation || multi_name(op, "randomkey") ||
           multi_name(op, "spop") || multi_name(op, "srandmember") ||
           multi_name(op, "zrandmember") || multi_name(op, "hrandfield") ||
           multi_name(op, "subscribe") || multi_name(op, "unsubscribe") ||
           multi_name(op, "psubscribe") || multi_name(op, "punsubscribe") ||
           multi_name(op, "ssubscribe") || multi_name(op, "sunsubscribe") ||
           multi_name(op, "acl");
}

bool has_name(const MultiQueuedCommand& queued, const char* lower) {
    return Slice(queued.argv[0].data(), static_cast<uint32_t>(queued.argv[0].size()))
        .eq_icase(lower);
}

MultiBlockingPop multi_blocking_pop(const MultiQueuedCommand& queued) {
    if (has_name(queued, "blpop")) return MultiBlockingPop::Blpop;
    if (has_name(queued, "brpop")) return MultiBlockingPop::Brpop;
    if (has_name(queued, "blmpop")) return MultiBlockingPop::Blmpop;
    if (has_name(queued, "bzpopmin")) return MultiBlockingPop::Bzpopmin;
    if (has_name(queued, "bzpopmax")) return MultiBlockingPop::Bzpopmax;
    if (has_name(queued, "bzmpop")) return MultiBlockingPop::Bzmpop;
    return MultiBlockingPop::None;
}

void command_key_args(const MultiQueuedCommand& queued, std::vector<uint32_t>& args) {
    const CommandSpec& spec = *queued.spec;
    if (spec.flags & CmdFlags::StreamRoute) {
        uint32_t streams = 1;
        while (streams < queued.argv.size() &&
               !Slice(queued.argv[streams].data(), queued.argv[streams].size()).eq_icase("streams"))
            streams++;
        if (streams == queued.argv.size() || ((queued.argv.size() - streams - 1) & 1u)) return;
        const uint32_t count = static_cast<uint32_t>((queued.argv.size() - streams - 1) / 2);
        for (uint32_t arg = streams + 1; arg < streams + 1 + count; arg++) args.push_back(arg);
        return;
    }
    const MultiBlockingPop blocking = multi_blocking_pop(queued);
    if (blocking == MultiBlockingPop::Blpop || blocking == MultiBlockingPop::Brpop ||
        blocking == MultiBlockingPop::Bzpopmin || blocking == MultiBlockingPop::Bzpopmax) {
        for (uint32_t arg = 1; arg + 1 < queued.argv.size(); arg++) args.push_back(arg);
        return;
    }
    if (blocking == MultiBlockingPop::Blmpop || blocking == MultiBlockingPop::Bzmpop) {
        int64_t parsed = 0;
        const Slice count(queued.argv[2].data(), static_cast<uint32_t>(queued.argv[2].size()));
        if (!parse_i64(count, parsed) || parsed < 1 ||
            static_cast<uint64_t>(parsed) > UINT32_MAX ||
            3 + static_cast<uint64_t>(parsed) >= queued.argv.size()) return;
        for (uint32_t arg = 3; arg < 3 + static_cast<uint32_t>(parsed); arg++)
            args.push_back(arg);
        return;
    }
    if (spec.first_key <= 0 || spec.key_step <= 0) return;
    const uint32_t last = spec.last_key < 0
        ? static_cast<uint32_t>(queued.argv.size() - 1)
        : std::min<uint32_t>(static_cast<uint32_t>(spec.last_key),
                             static_cast<uint32_t>(queued.argv.size() - 1));
    for (uint32_t arg = static_cast<uint32_t>(spec.first_key); arg <= last;
         arg += static_cast<uint32_t>(spec.key_step))
        args.push_back(arg);
    // SORT'S STORE DESTINATION IS AN OPTION WORD, NOT PART OF ITS REGISTRY KEY RANGE (1..1), so the
    // loop above misses it. A queued `SORT src STORE dst` therefore looked like a ONE-key command:
    // classify_multi_command() saw a single shard, called it Local, and EXEC ran the same-owner arm
    // on the SOURCE's shard -- which installed `dst` in the source's table. The key was then
    // invisible to every routed lookup (EXISTS/TYPE/LRANGE answer on dst's real owner) while KEYS
    // and DBSIZE still counted it, and a snapshot would have persisted it under the wrong shard.
    // Naming the destination here restores the ordinary lowering: same shard stays Local and is
    // correct; different shards fall through to xshard_prepare's two-hop apply. It also puts the
    // destination into add_write_key(), so WATCH on it now sees the write.
    // SORT_RO is excluded by name: STORE is a syntax error there, so it names no destination.
    if (has_name(queued, "sort")) {
        uint32_t store_arg = 0;
        for (uint32_t i = 2; i < queued.argv.size(); i++) {
            const Slice word(queued.argv[i].data(),
                             static_cast<uint32_t>(queued.argv[i].size()));
            // Mirror parse_sort_options' grammar exactly, because a BY or GET pattern may itself
            // be the word STORE and must not be mistaken for the option.
            if (word.eq_icase("limit") && i + 2 < queued.argv.size()) i += 2;
            else if ((word.eq_icase("by") || word.eq_icase("get")) && i + 1 < queued.argv.size()) i++;
            else if (word.eq_icase("store") && i + 1 < queued.argv.size()) store_arg = ++i;
        }
        if (store_arg) args.push_back(store_arg);   // last STORE wins, as the parser records it
    }
}

// True when a queued SORT will READ keys derived from its elements. Such a command touches shards
// that no key of the transaction names, so it cannot be executed as an ordinary one-key Local child:
// see the participation note in prepare_commands().
bool multi_sort_dereferences(const MultiQueuedCommand& queued) {
    if (!has_name(queued, "sort") && !has_name(queued, "sort_ro")) return false;
    const uint32_t argc = static_cast<uint32_t>(queued.argv.size());
    for (uint32_t i = 2; i < argc; i++) {
        const Slice word(queued.argv[i].data(), static_cast<uint32_t>(queued.argv[i].size()));
        // Mirror parse_sort_options' grammar so an option word appearing INSIDE a pattern is not
        // mistaken for the option itself.
        if (word.eq_icase("limit") && i + 2 < argc) { i += 2; continue; }
        if (!(word.eq_icase("by") || word.eq_icase("get")) || i + 1 >= argc) continue;
        const std::string& pattern = queued.argv[++i];
        // `#` is the element and a pattern with no '*' is a constant nil: neither reads a key.
        const bool self = word.eq_icase("get") && pattern.size() == 1 && pattern[0] == '#';
        if (!self && pattern.find('*') != std::string::npos) return true;
    }
    return false;
}

bool contains_shard(const std::vector<int32_t>& shards, int32_t shard) {
    return std::find(shards.begin(), shards.end(), shard) != shards.end();
}

void add_shard(std::vector<int32_t>& shards, int32_t shard) {
    if (!contains_shard(shards, shard)) shards.push_back(shard);
}

bool multi_xshard_stage_has_group(const MultiCommand& command, uint32_t stage, int32_t shard) {
    if (stage >= MultiCommand::kXshardStages || shard < 0 || shard >= 256) std::abort();
    const uint32_t sid = static_cast<uint32_t>(shard);
    return command.xshard_stage_groups[stage][sid >> 6] & (1ull << (sid & 63));
}

bool make_child_op(MultiCommand& command) {
    command.op = std::make_unique<Op>();
    command.op->reset();
    command.op->spec = command.queued.spec;
    for (const std::string& arg : command.queued.argv)
        if (!command.op->push_arg(Slice(arg.data(), static_cast<uint32_t>(arg.size()))))
            return false;
    return true;
}

bool validate_multi_blocking_timeout(Op& op, MultiBlockingPop kind) {
    const uint32_t timeout_arg = (kind == MultiBlockingPop::Blmpop ||
                                  kind == MultiBlockingPop::Bzmpop)
        ? 1 : op.argc() - 1;
    int64_t timeout_ms = 0;
    if (blocking_reply_timeout_error(op, parse_timeout_ms(op.arg(timeout_arg), timeout_ms)))
        return false;
    if (timeout_ms != 0) {
        timespec now{};
        ::clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME, &now);
        const int64_t now_ms = static_cast<int64_t>(now.tv_sec) * 1000 + now.tv_nsec / 1000000;
        if (timeout_ms > INT64_MAX - now_ms) {
            reply_err(op.sink(), "ERR timeout is out of range");
            return false;
        }
    }
    return true;
}

bool normalize_multi_blocking_pop(MultiCommand& command) {
    const MultiBlockingPop kind = command.blocking_pop;
    const bool list = kind == MultiBlockingPop::Blpop || kind == MultiBlockingPop::Brpop ||
                      kind == MultiBlockingPop::Blmpop;
    const bool single = kind == MultiBlockingPop::Blpop || kind == MultiBlockingPop::Brpop ||
                        kind == MultiBlockingPop::Bzpopmin || kind == MultiBlockingPop::Bzpopmax;
    const char* alias = list ? "LMPOP" : "ZMPOP";
    const CommandSpec* spec = command_lookup(Slice(alias, 5));
    if (!spec) return false;
    if (command.queued.spec->flags & CmdFlags::NotifySelected)
        spec = command_notify_variant(spec);

    command.exec_argv.clear();
    if (single) {
        command.exec_argv.reserve(command.queued.argv.size() + 3);
        command.exec_argv.emplace_back(alias);
        command.exec_argv.push_back(std::to_string(command.queued.argv.size() - 2));
        for (uint32_t i = 1; i + 1 < command.queued.argv.size(); i++)
            command.exec_argv.push_back(command.queued.argv[i]);
        const bool right_or_max = kind == MultiBlockingPop::Brpop ||
                                  kind == MultiBlockingPop::Bzpopmax;
        command.exec_argv.emplace_back(list ? (right_or_max ? "RIGHT" : "LEFT")
                                            : (right_or_max ? "MAX" : "MIN"));
        command.exec_argv.emplace_back("COUNT");
        command.exec_argv.emplace_back("1");
        command.pop_reply_shape = static_cast<uint8_t>(
            list ? PopReplyShape::ListPair : PopReplyShape::ZsetTriple);
    } else {
        command.exec_argv.reserve(command.queued.argv.size() - 1);
        command.exec_argv.emplace_back(alias);
        for (uint32_t i = 2; i < command.queued.argv.size(); i++)
            command.exec_argv.push_back(command.queued.argv[i]);
        command.pop_reply_shape = static_cast<uint8_t>(PopReplyShape::Mpop);
    }

    command.op->reset();
    command.op->spec = spec;
    for (const std::string& arg : command.exec_argv)
        if (!command.op->push_arg(Slice(arg.data(), static_cast<uint32_t>(arg.size()))))
            return false;
    return true;
}

MultiCommandKind classify_multi_command(MultiCommand& command) {
    if (has_name(command.queued, "ping")) return MultiCommandKind::Ping;
    if (has_name(command.queued, "echo")) return MultiCommandKind::Echo;
    if (has_name(command.queued, "unwatch")) return MultiCommandKind::UnwatchReply;
    if (command.queued.spec->flags & CmdFlags::ConnLocal) return MultiCommandKind::IoLocal;
    if (has_name(command.queued, "dbsize")) return MultiCommandKind::IoLocal;
    if (has_name(command.queued, "config") && command.queued.argv.size() > 1 &&
        Slice(command.queued.argv[1].data(),
              static_cast<uint32_t>(command.queued.argv[1].size())).eq_icase("get"))
        return MultiCommandKind::IoLocal;
    // SubcmdRoute containers ride CursorShard only to reach the IO special-route hook; they are
    // not cursor commands. Their keyed forms have a truthful key range and fall through to Local;
    // their keyless subcommands answer on the IO thread like DBSIZE and CONFIG GET.
    if (command.queued.spec->flags & CmdFlags::SubcmdRoute)
        return command.key_args.empty() ? MultiCommandKind::IoLocal : MultiCommandKind::Local;
    if ((command.queued.spec->flags & CmdFlags::CursorShard) &&
        !(command.queued.spec->flags & CmdFlags::StreamRoute)) return MultiCommandKind::Scan;
    // These six execute through a normalized nonblocking xshard child even when all keys happen
    // to share one owner. Calling their ordinary Blocking handler from EXEC would park the whole
    // transaction, which Redis never does.
    if (command.blocking_pop != MultiBlockingPop::None) return MultiCommandKind::Unsupported;
    if (command.key_args.empty()) return MultiCommandKind::Unsupported;
    // A DEREFERENCING SORT IS NEVER LOCAL, however few keys it names. Its BY/GET patterns read keys
    // derived from the source's ELEMENTS, on shards this transaction never declared, and a Local
    // child is ordered only against the commands that share its one shard -- so an earlier MSET
    // still pending on a weight key's shard would be invisible to it. As an Xshard child it can
    // declare every shard as a participant and take the transaction's ordinary stage barrier.
    if (multi_sort_dereferences(command.queued)) return MultiCommandKind::Unsupported;
    bool same = true;
    for (size_t i = 1; i < command.key_shards.size(); i++)
        same &= command.key_shards[i] == command.key_shards[0];
    if (same) return MultiCommandKind::Local;
    if (has_name(command.queued, "mget")) return MultiCommandKind::Mget;
    if (has_name(command.queued, "mset")) return MultiCommandKind::Mset;
    if (has_name(command.queued, "msetnx")) return MultiCommandKind::Msetnx;
    if (has_name(command.queued, "del") || has_name(command.queued, "unlink"))
        return MultiCommandKind::Del;
    if (has_name(command.queued, "exists") || has_name(command.queued, "touch"))
        return MultiCommandKind::Exists;
    return MultiCommandKind::Unsupported;
}

bool state_writes_key(const MultiExecState& state, const MultiWatchedKey& watched) {
    for (const MultiWriteKey& key : state.write_keys)
        if (key.shard == watched.shard && key.key == watched.key) return true;
    return false;
}

void add_write_key(MultiExecState& state, const MultiCommand& command, uint32_t index) {
    if (!(command.queued.spec->flags & (CmdFlags::Write | CmdFlags::SnapshotWrite))) return;
    if (command.kind == MultiCommandKind::Unsupported) return;
    const uint32_t arg = command.key_args[index];
    const std::string& key = command.queued.argv[arg];
    const int32_t shard = command.key_shards[index];
    MultiWriteKey candidate{
        key, FlatStore::hash_key(Slice(key.data(), static_cast<uint32_t>(key.size()))), shard};
    if (!state.write_key_set.emplace(candidate).second) return;
    state.write_keys.push_back(std::move(candidate));
}

bool command_has_owner_work(const MultiCommand& command);

            }
