WorkError begin_plain_version(Server& server, Shard& shard, Slice key, uint64_t hash,
                              uint64_t snapshot, uint64_t origin_conn_id) {
    // Cleanup is owner-pass work: every caller has already made the pass's single promotion
    // attempt before asking individual keys whether they still need a version.
    FlatStore& store = shard.store();
    const bool had_record = store.atomic_has_record(hash, key);
    // A key reserved by a staged cross-owner script carries no MVCC record of its own, so the
    // record test alone sent this write down the untracked physical path -- it mutated the value
    // in place, drew no ticket, and left the script's APPLY-side validation nothing to detect.
    // The reservation is exactly a demand that this branch be taken.
    const bool script_forced = !had_record && store.atomic_has_script_intent(hash, key);
    if (!had_record && !script_forced) {
        if (snapshot != UINT64_MAX) store.atomic_set_read_context(snapshot, origin_conn_id);
        return WorkError::None;
    }
    if (script_forced) server.note_script_forced_write();

    if (snapshot == UINT64_MAX) snapshot = server.atomic_snapshot();
    store.atomic_set_read_context(snapshot, origin_conn_id);
    KvObj* visible = store.find(hash, key);
    KvObj* clone = nullptr;
    if (visible) {
        ObjectImage image;
        if (!serialize_object(visible, image)) {
            store.atomic_clear_read_epoch();
            return WorkError::Oom;
        }
        const SnapshotHookStatus loaded = load_object_image(
            key, image, shard.type_limits(), clone);
        if (loaded != SnapshotHookStatus::Ok || !clone) {
            store.atomic_clear_read_epoch();
            return loaded == SnapshotHookStatus::Oom ? WorkError::Oom : WorkError::Corrupt;
        }
    }

    void* prepared = nullptr;
    if (!store.atomic_prepare_plain(key, hash, origin_conn_id, prepared) ||
        !store.atomic_prepare_capacity(1) || !store.atomic_admit(key, clone)) {
        if (prepared) store.atomic_discard_plain(prepared);
        if (clone) kvobj_free(clone);
        store.atomic_clear_read_epoch();
        return WorkError::Oom;
    }
    const uint64_t ticket = server.atomic_commit();
    store.atomic_install_plain(hash, key, prepared, clone, ticket);
    return WorkError::None;
}

ScatterTaskResult execute_atomic_direct_rename(const Task& task, Shard& shard, Op& op,
                                               uint32_t owner_thread_id) {
    ScatterState& state = *task.scatter;
    ShardGroup& group = *group_for(state, shard.id());
    bool source_group = false;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < group.count; i++)
        source_group |= state.key_order[group.begin + i] == 0;

    if (!source_group) {
        const uint8_t ready = state.direct_ready.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
        if (ready == 0) return ScatterTaskResult::Retry;
        if (ready == 2 || state.aborted.load(std::memory_order_acquire))
            return ScatterTaskResult::Complete;
        return execute_atomic_apply(task, shard, op, owner_thread_id);
    }

    const KeyRef& source_key = state.keys[0];
    KvObj* source = shard.store().find(source_key.hash, op.arg(source_key.arg));
    if (!source) {
        state.final_reply = FinalReply::NoSuchKey;
        state.aborted.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
        state.direct_ready.store(2, std::memory_order_release);
        return ScatterTaskResult::Complete;
    }

    KeyRef& destination_key = state.keys[1];
    ObjectImage& destination = state.apply[1];
    destination.present = true;
    destination.type = static_cast<Type>(source->type);
    destination.expire_at_ms = source->expire_at_ms();
    KvObj* clone = nullptr;
    if (destination.type == Type::String) {
        KvObjRawReadBuffer raw;
        clone = source->is_int()
            ? kvobj_new_int(op.arg(destination_key.arg), source->int_value(),
                            destination.expire_at_ms, source->has_ttl_slot())
            : xshard_make_string(op.arg(destination_key.arg),
                                 kvobj_string_value(source, raw),
                                 destination.expire_at_ms, false,
                                 source->has_ttl_slot());
    } else {
        if (!serialize_object(source, destination)) {
            group.error = WorkError::Oom;
        } else {
            const SnapshotHookStatus loaded = load_object_image(
                op.arg(destination_key.arg), destination, shard.type_limits(), clone);
            if (loaded != SnapshotHookStatus::Ok || !clone)
                group.error = loaded == SnapshotHookStatus::Oom
                    ? WorkError::Oom : WorkError::Corrupt;
        }
    }
    if (!clone || group.error != WorkError::None) {
        if (clone) kvobj_free(clone);
        if (group.error == WorkError::None) group.error = WorkError::Oom;
        state.aborted.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
        state.direct_ready.store(2, std::memory_order_release);
        return ScatterTaskResult::Complete;
    }
    destination_key.stable_object = clone;
    destination_key.key_anchor = clone;
    state.direct_ready.store(1, std::memory_order_release);
    return execute_atomic_apply(task, shard, op, owner_thread_id);
}

ScatterTaskResult execute_atomic_apply(const Task& task, Shard& shard, Op& op,
                                       uint32_t owner_thread_id) {
    ScatterState& state = *task.scatter;
    ShardGroup& group = *group_for(state, shard.id());
        case XshardElementResult::Missing: return WorkError::None;
        case XshardElementResult::WrongType: return WorkError::WrongType;
        case XshardElementResult::Oom: return WorkError::Oom;
        case XshardElementResult::Maxmemory: return WorkError::Maxmemory;
        case XshardElementResult::InsertFailed: return WorkError::InsertFailed;
    }
    return WorkError::InsertFailed;
}

}  // namespace

struct alignas(64) OwnerRecordRefs {
    // A slot is touched only by its executor: every shard mapped to one owner is serialized there.
    // Cache-line spacing prevents cleanup on distinct owners from bouncing a shared counter line.
    // A pre-counted standalone wave starts nodes at one. That completion sentinel prevents cleanup
    // of an early-aborted entry from taking the count to zero before the owner's last task runs.
    uint32_t nodes = 0;
    uint32_t remaining = 0;
    uint32_t group_count = 0;
};

// The read cut lives in the shared SnapshotCut base so a transaction can hold one through the
// same per-IO-thread floor arithmetic (see xshard.h).  Member names are unchanged, so every
// state->snapshot / state->snapshot_registered reference below still resolves.
struct ScatterState : SnapshotCut {
    ~ScatterState() { notify_discard_batch(notify.exchange(nullptr)); }
    std::atomic<uint32_t> pending{0};
    // Pending group entries may retain this state after reply retirement, hence record_refs.
    std::atomic<uint32_t> record_refs{0};
    // A watched-key reservation names the group decision too.  It holds this second lifetime pin
    // until its owner shard consumes the published decision, including groups that install no
    // MVCC record (for example a failed conditional write).
    std::atomic<uint32_t> watch_refs{0};
    std::atomic<bool> conditional_failed{false};
    std::atomic<bool> script_conflict{false};
    std::atomic<uint8_t> direct_ready{0};     // 0=source pending, 1=image ready, 2=terminal
    std::atomic<uint64_t> exact_sum{0};
    Kind kind = Kind::AllShards;
    FinalReply final_reply = FinalReply::None;
    WorkError final_error = WorkError::None;
    uint8_t phase = 1;
    ScriptPhase script_phase = ScriptPhase::None;
    // Set when a wave could not find task slots and the poster is holding its own `pending`
    // reference across the requeue. While it is set no owner task may execute a phase body: the
    // phase word already names the wave that is still being published.
    bool script_resume_post = false;
    bool script_pins_live = false;
    bool script_ticket_live = false;
    bool script_apply_after_unpin = false;
    bool script_commit_after_unpin = false;
    bool script_has_writes = false;
    bool script_stage_limit = false;
    bool script_certifier = false;
    bool runtime_loading = false;
    // Set for a child lowered inside EXEC. The child keeps its own decision words, but the parent
    // publishes their common ticket and owns the outer transaction decision.
    bool multi_child = false;
    bool barrier = false;
    bool pooled = false;
    bool copy_replace = false;
    bool from_left = false;
    bool to_left = false;
    bool pop_edge = false;                 // RIGHT for LMPOP, MAX for ZMPOP
    PopReplyShape pop_reply_shape = PopReplyShape::Mpop;
    bool atomic_write = false;
    bool atomic_apply = false;
    bool atomic_pop = false;
    bool atomic_group = false;
    bool atomic_direct = false;
    bool pop_missed = false;
    // SORT's general form is computed on an executor. Dereferencing forms set this only after the
    // last owner-grouped gather task has returned; non-dereferencing forms may set it in the source
    // task. Completion consumes the one result in either case.
    bool sort_general_done = false;
    bool sort_conversion_error = false;
    bool admitted = false;
    // True between admission and the moment this group's records are installed on every owner.
    // See Server::atomic_apply_inflight() for why the snapshot cut waits on this and not on the
    // admission lease.
    std::atomic<bool> apply_open{false};
    // A MULTI child's records deliberately point at the CHILD epoch/abort words: a runtime error
    // cancels that one queued command without turning the whole EXEC into EXECABORT. The parent
    // finalizer installs one common ticket into every successful decision word before advancing
    // the safe watermark.
    bool contents_freed = false;
    bool retired = false;
    // but a stale id is the kind of thing the next handler quietly inherits. Re-stamping also
    // picks up live CONFIG SET changes to the type/stream limits.
    if (workbench->id() != coordinator)
        workbench->init_private(&server, coordinator, server.cfg().type_limits,
                                server.cfg().stream_limits);
    return workbench;
}

struct ScriptAccessScope {
    explicit ScriptAccessScope(Op& op, uint8_t* access, uint32_t count) {
        script_cross_access_begin(op, access, count);
    }
    ~ScriptAccessScope() { script_cross_access_end(); }
};

ScatterTaskResult execute_script_phase(const Task& task, Shard& shard, Op& op) {
    ScatterState& state = *task.scatter;
    ShardGroup* group = group_for(state, shard.id());
    if (state.script_resume_post) return ScatterTaskResult::Complete;
    if (!group && state.script_phase != ScriptPhase::Run) std::abort();

    switch (state.script_phase) {
        case ScriptPhase::Pin: {
            for (uint32_t i = 0; i < group->count; i++) {
                const uint32_t pos = state.key_order[group->begin + i];
                const KeyRef& key = state.keys[pos];
                if (state.aborted.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) break;
#ifdef TOMO_XSCRIPT_NO_RESERVE
                // NEGATIVE-CONTROL BUILD ONLY (make noreserve). Everything else about the
                // activation is unchanged -- same waves, same cut, same validation -- so a battery
                // that passes here is a battery that was never testing the reservation.
                continue;
#endif
                if (!shard.store().atomic_script_pin(key.hash, op.arg(key.arg))) {
                    group->error = WorkError::Oom;
                    state.aborted.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
                    break;
                }
                state.server->note_script_key_armed();
                state.script_pinned[pos] = 1;
            }
            return ScatterTaskResult::Complete;
        }
        case ScriptPhase::Read: {
            if (state.aborted.load(std::memory_order_acquire))
                return ScatterTaskResult::Complete;
            // The owner's expiry cut is already state.now_cut_ms: xshard_execute installed it
            // before dispatching this phase, and it is the same instant every other owner of this
            // script is reading against.
            shard.store().atomic_set_read_context(state.script_cut, state.origin_conn_id);
            uint64_t local_bytes = 0;
            for (uint32_t i = 0; i < group->count; i++) {
                const uint32_t pos = state.key_order[group->begin + i];
                const KeyRef& key = state.keys[pos];
                KvObj* value = shard.store().find(key.hash, op.arg(key.arg));
                if (!serialize_object(value, state.images[pos])) {
                    group->error = WorkError::Oom;
                    state.aborted.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
                    break;
                }
                local_bytes += sizeof(ObjectImage) + op.arg(key.arg).n +
                               state.images[pos].payload.size();
            }
            shard.store().atomic_clear_read_epoch();
            const uint64_t total = state.script_staged_bytes.fetch_add(
                local_bytes, std::memory_order_relaxed) + local_bytes;
            state.server->note_script_stage_owner(local_bytes);
            if (total > state.server->script_crossshard_max_bytes()) {
                state.script_stage_limit = true;
                group->error = WorkError::Oom;
                state.aborted.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
            }
            return ScatterTaskResult::Complete;
        }
        case ScriptPhase::Run: {
            state.server->note_script_run();
            Shard* work = script_workbench(*state.server, state.script_coordinator_shard);
            work->store().clear();
            // The workbench is a shard object of its own, so xshard_execute's cut does not reach
            // it; give it the same instant explicitly.
            work->pin_now_ms(state.now_cut_ms);
            for (uint32_t pos = 0; pos < state.key_count; pos++) {
                const KeyRef& key = state.keys[pos];
                const WorkError loaded = apply_image<false>(
                    *work, op.arg(key.arg), key.hash, state.images[pos], true);
                if (loaded != WorkError::None) {
                    state.final_error = loaded;
                    state.aborted.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
                    return ScatterTaskResult::Complete;
                }
            }
            if (work->store().object_bytes() >
                state.server->script_crossshard_workbench_bytes()) {
                state.final_error = WorkError::Maxmemory;
                state.aborted.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
                return ScatterTaskResult::Complete;
            }
            op.clear_reply();
            const uint64_t workbench_hits = work->stats().hits;
            const uint64_t workbench_misses = work->stats().misses;
            {
                ScriptAccessScope access(op, state.status, state.key_count);
                op.spec->handler(*work, op);
            }
            // The workbench is intentionally absent from Server::shards(), so forward the nested
            // command's read-lookup counters to the real coordinator shard before it is reused.
            shard.stats().hits += work->stats().hits - workbench_hits;
            shard.stats().misses += work->stats().misses - workbench_misses;
            if (work->store().object_bytes() >
                state.server->script_crossshard_workbench_bytes()) {
                state.final_error = WorkError::Maxmemory;
                state.aborted.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
                return ScatterTaskResult::Complete;
            }
            for (uint32_t pos = 0; pos < state.key_count; pos++) {
                if (!(state.status[pos] & 2u)) continue;
                const KeyRef& key = state.keys[pos];
                KvObj* value = work->store().find(key.hash, op.arg(key.arg));
                if (!serialize_object(value, state.apply[pos])) {
                    state.final_error = WorkError::Oom;
                    state.aborted.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
                    break;
                }
            }
            return ScatterTaskResult::Complete;
        }
        case ScriptPhase::Validate:
            state.server->note_script_validate_owner();
            for (uint32_t i = 0; i < group->count; i++) {
                const uint32_t pos = state.key_order[group->begin + i];
                const KeyRef& key = state.keys[pos];
                if (shard.store().atomic_script_changed(
                        key.hash, op.arg(key.arg), state.script_cut)) {
                    state.script_conflict.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
                    break;
                }
            }
            return ScatterTaskResult::Complete;
        case ScriptPhase::Unpin:
            for (uint32_t i = 0; i < group->count; i++) {
                const uint32_t pos = state.key_order[group->begin + i];
                if (!state.script_pinned[pos]) continue;
                const KeyRef& key = state.keys[pos];
                shard.store().atomic_script_unpin(key.hash, op.arg(key.arg));
                state.server->note_script_key_released();
                state.script_pinned[pos] = 0;
            }
            return ScatterTaskResult::Complete;
        case ScriptPhase::Apply:
        case ScriptPhase::None:
            break;
    }
    return ScatterTaskResult::Complete;
}

bool xshard_owner_mutation_phase(const ScatterState& state, const Op& op) {
    if (state.kind == Kind::Script && state.script_resume_post) return false;
    if (!(op.spec->flags & (CmdFlags::Write | CmdFlags::SnapshotWrite))) return false;
    if (state.atomic_write) return true;
    if (state.atomic_apply || state.atomic_pop || state.two_hop) return state.phase == 2;
    return true;
}

}  // namespace

void xshard_visit_task_hashes(const Task& task, void* context,
    if (!group) return;
    if (sort_deref_gathering(state)) {
        const SortDerefState& sort = *state.sort_deref;
        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < group->count; i++)
            visit(context, sort.requests[sort.key_order[group->begin + i]].hash);
        return;
    }
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < group->count; i++)
        visit(context, state.keys[state.key_order[group->begin + i]].hash);
}

ScatterTaskResult xshard_execute(const Task& task, Shard& shard, Op& op,
                                 uint32_t owner_thread_id) {
    const bool notify = (op.spec->flags & CmdFlags::NotifySelected) != 0;
    NotifyExecutionScope notify_scope(shard, op, notify, shard.notify_order_base());
    ScatterState& state = *task.scatter;
    // ONE EXPIRY CUT FOR THE WHOLE FAN-OUT. Before this, each fragment compared deadlines against
    // its own executor's per-pass clock, so an eight-owner MGET could report a key alive on one
    // owner and elapsed on another -- a keyspace that existed at no instant. Cheap enough to be
    // unconditional on the cross-shard path: two stores in, two out, and single-shard commands
    // never reach this function at all.
    PinnedNowMs now_cut(shard, state.now_cut_ms);
    if (state.kind == Kind::Script &&
        (state.script_phase != ScriptPhase::Apply || state.script_resume_post))
        return execute_script_phase(task, shard, op);
    ShardGroup& group = *group_for(state, shard.id());
    if (xshard_owner_mutation_phase(state, op) && shard.has_watches()) {
        const void* token = state.atomic_group ? static_cast<const void*>(&state) : nullptr;
        if (group.count == 0) {
            if (!shard.watch_all_write_ready()) return ScatterTaskResult::Retry;
        } else {
            for (uint32_t i = 0; i < group.count; i++) {
                const uint32_t pos = state.key_order[group.begin + i];
                const KeyRef& key = state.keys[pos];
                if (!shard.watch_write_ready(op.arg(key.arg), token))
                    return ScatterTaskResult::Retry;
            }
            if (state.atomic_group) {
                for (uint32_t i = 0; i < group.count; i++) {
                    const uint32_t pos = state.key_order[group.begin + i];
                    const KeyRef& key = state.keys[pos];
                    shard.watch_reserve_write(
                        op.arg(key.arg), task.client, task.client->watch_generation(), &state,
                        publish_epoch(state), publish_aborted(state), &state.watch_refs);
                }
            }
        }
    }
    // The executor-wide batch prefetch deliberately excludes scatter tasks. Recover their structural
    // advantage here, after routing has made the batch owner-local and before MVCC promotion or the
    // ordinary gather serializes the same storage accesses. Atomic writes prepare capacity first
    // below because that preparation may change table geometry.
    if (!state.atomic_write) prefetch_owner_group(shard.store(), state, group);
    if (!state.atomic_write && shard.store().atomic_has_records()) {
        const uint64_t cleanup_cutoff = state.server->atomic_snapshot();
        const uint64_t floor = state.server->atomic_read_floor();
        if (sort_deref_gathering(state)) {
            SortDerefState& sort = *state.sort_deref;
            shard.store().atomic_promote_keys(
                group.count, group.membership, floor, cleanup_cutoff, [&](uint32_t i) {
                    const SortDerefRequest& request =
                        sort.requests[sort.key_order[group.begin + i]];
                    return std::pair<uint64_t, Slice>{request.hash, sort_deref_key(request)};
                });
        } else {
            shard.store().atomic_promote_keys(
                group.count, group.membership, floor, cleanup_cutoff, [&](uint32_t i) {
                    const uint32_t pos = state.key_order[group.begin + i];
                    const KeyRef& key = state.keys[pos];
                    return std::pair<uint64_t, Slice>{key.hash, op.arg(key.arg)};
                });
        }
    }
    struct ReadEpochGuard {
        FlatStore& store;
        bool bound;
        ReadEpochGuard(FlatStore& store_, uint64_t snapshot, uint64_t origin_conn_id)
            : store(store_), bound(snapshot != UINT64_MAX) {
            if (bound) store.atomic_set_read_context(snapshot, origin_conn_id);
        }
        ~ReadEpochGuard() { if (bound) store.atomic_clear_read_epoch(); }
    };
    const uint64_t read_snapshot = state.atomic_pop && state.phase == 1 &&
                                   state.pop_retry_snapshot != UINT64_MAX
        ? state.pop_retry_snapshot : state.snapshot;
    const bool read_latest = state.atomic_direct || (state.atomic_pop && state.phase == 2);
    ReadEpochGuard read_epoch(
        shard.store(), read_latest ? UINT64_MAX : read_snapshot, state.origin_conn_id);
    try {
        if (state.atomic_direct)
            return execute_atomic_direct_rename(task, shard, op, owner_thread_id);
        if (state.atomic_apply && state.phase == 2) {
            if (state.kind == Kind::Script) state.server->note_script_apply_owner();
            return execute_atomic_apply(task, shard, op, owner_thread_id);
        }
        if (state.atomic_write) {
            // One owner pass preflights the table, allocates one shard entry, and performs ordinary
            // physical replacements. Per key, the entry records only the displaced pointer.
            if (!shard.store().atomic_prepare_capacity(group.count)) {
            prefetch_owner_group(shard.store(), state, group);
            // MSETNX tests the pre-command state. Duplicate keys in one command are not an
            // existence failure (Redis installs the last supplied value); probing after the first
            // physical exchange would see our own still-private candidate because the entry is
            // intentionally linked only after the complete shard pass. Preflight every local key
            // before any exchange, then materialize the whole candidate span.
            if (state.kind == Kind::Msetnx) {
                for (uint32_t i = 0; i < group.count; i++) {
                    const uint32_t pos = state.key_order[group.begin + i];
                    const KeyRef& key = state.keys[pos];
                    if (notify ? shard.store_find<true>(key.hash, op.arg(key.arg))
                               : shard.store().find(key.hash, op.arg(key.arg))) {
                        state.aborted.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
                        shard.store().atomic_discard_group(pending_entry);
                        return ScatterTaskResult::Complete;
                    }
                }
            }
            // Atomic string installs bypass FlatStore::insert(). Keep the common path to one
            // predicted-cold gate; only an enabled n class performs the visibility probes. The
            // records remain on the scatter sidecar and are discarded if the group later aborts.
            if (notify && __builtin_expect(notify_flat_enabled(&shard, NOTIFY_NEW), false) &&
                (state.kind == Kind::Mset || state.kind == Kind::Msetnx)) {
                for (uint32_t i = 0; i < group.count; i++) {
                    const uint32_t pos = state.key_order[group.begin + i];
                    const KeyRef& key = state.keys[pos];
                    const Slice key_slice = op.arg(key.arg);
                    bool duplicate = false;
                    for (uint32_t prior = 0; prior < i; prior++) {
                        const uint32_t p = state.key_order[group.begin + prior];
                        duplicate = state.keys[p].hash == key.hash &&
                                    op.arg(state.keys[p].arg) == key_slice;
                        if (duplicate) break;
                    }
                    if (!duplicate && !shard.store().atomic_find_tracked(key.hash, key_slice))
                        notify_record(shard, op, NOTIFY_NEW, NotifyEventId::New, key_slice);
                }
            }
            for (uint32_t i = 0; i < group.count; i++) {
                const uint32_t pos = state.key_order[group.begin + i];
                KeyRef& key = state.keys[pos];
                const Slice key_slice = op.arg(key.arg);
                KvObj* visible = (state.kind == Kind::Mset || state.kind == Kind::Msetnx)
                    ? nullptr : (notify ? shard.store_find<true>(key.hash, key_slice)
                                        : shard.store().find(key.hash, key_slice));
                if (state.kind == Kind::Del || state.kind == Kind::Unlink) {
                    bool duplicate = false;
                    for (uint32_t prior = 0; prior < i; prior++) {
                        const uint32_t p = state.key_order[group.begin + prior];
                        const Slice prior_key = op.arg(state.keys[p].arg);
                        duplicate = state.keys[p].hash == key.hash && prior_key == key_slice;
                        if (duplicate) break;
                    }
                    state.status[pos] = visible && !duplicate;
                    // DEL installs no object of its own. atomic_install_group copies key identity
                    // into this owner span's packed record tail before the record is published.
                    KvObj* old = shard.store().atomic_install_group(
                        pending_entry, key.hash, key_slice, nullptr);
                    if (old) parked_bytes += kvobj_size(old);
                    installed++;
                    continue;
                }

                KvObj* value = key.key_anchor;
                const bool io_prebuilt = value != nullptr;
                if (io_prebuilt && key.stable_object != value) std::abort();
                if (!value) {
                    value = xshard_make_atomic_string(
                        shard, key_slice, op.arg(key.arg + 1));
                    if (!value) {
                        group.error = WorkError::Oom;
                        state.aborted.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
                        break;
                    }
                }
                if (!shard.store().atomic_admit(key_slice, value)) {
                    if (!io_prebuilt) shard.store().atomic_discard_value(value);
                    group.error = WorkError::Maxmemory;
                    state.aborted.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
                    break;
                }
                key.stable_object = value;
                KvObj* old = shard.store().atomic_install_group(
                    pending_entry, key.hash, key_slice, value);
                if (old) parked_bytes += kvobj_size(old);
                installed_bytes += kvobj_size(value);
                if (io_prebuilt) key.key_anchor = nullptr;
                installed++;
            }
            if (installed) {
                shard.store().atomic_finish_group_install(parked_bytes, installed_bytes);
                shard.store().atomic_publish_group(pending_entry);
                note_owner_record_install(state, *owner_refs);
            } else {
                shard.store().atomic_discard_group(pending_entry);
            }
            return ScatterTaskResult::Complete;
        }

        const bool pending_reads = shard.store().atomic_has_records();
        if (__builtin_expect(atomic_tripwire_enabled(), false))
            xshard_tripwire_fragment_execute(
                task, shard, op, !pending_reads, read_latest ? UINT64_MAX : read_snapshot);
        auto find_value = [&](uint64_t hash, Slice key, bool read_lookup = false) {
            KvObj* object = pending_reads ? shard.store().atomic_find_tracked(hash, key)
                                          : (notify ? shard.store_find<true>(hash, key)
                                                    : shard.store().find(hash, key));
            if (read_lookup) shard.note_keyspace_read(object);
            return object;
        };

        // SORT's second read wave has concrete keys but no argv positions. Each request is executed
        // only by its routed owner, under the ReadEpochGuard and PinnedNowMs installed above.
        if (sort_deref_gathering(state)) {
            SortDerefState& sort = *state.sort_deref;
            for (uint32_t i = 0; i < group.count; i++) {
                SortDerefRequest& request = sort.requests[sort.key_order[group.begin + i]];
                const Slice key = sort_deref_key(request);
                state.server->note_sort_deref_lookup();
                KvObj* object = find_value(request.hash, key, true);
                if (!object) continue;

exec
/bin/bash -lc "sed -n '3370,3665p' src/cmd/scatter_engine.inc && sed -n '125,260p' src/cmd/atomics_glue.inc && sed -n '390,485p' src/store/flatstore_atomic.inc && rg -n 'suspend.*evict|evict.*suspend|multi_child_bind|multi_child.*snapshot' src/cmd src/store/flatstore.h" in /home/user/Projects/cx-fix-atomics
 succeeded in 0ms:
                    state.server->note_sort_scatter_general();
                }
                return ScatterTaskResult::Complete;
        }
    } catch (const std::bad_alloc&) {
        group.error = WorkError::Oom;
        return ScatterTaskResult::Complete;
    }
}

void script_snapshot_done(Server& server, ScatterState& state) {
    if (state.snapshot_registered &&
        !state.snapshot_complete.exchange(true, std::memory_order_acq_rel))
        server.note_atomic_snapshot_complete(state.owner_io);
}

void script_engine_error_reply(Op& op, ScatterState& state, WorkError error) {
    op.clear_reply();
    if (state.script_stage_limit) {
        reply_err(op.sink(), "ERR cross-shard script staging limit exceeded");
    } else if (error == WorkError::Maxmemory) {
        reply_maxmemory_oom(op);
    } else {
        reply_work_error(op, error == WorkError::None ? WorkError::Oom : error);
    }
}

// Drives one activation from wave to wave. Exactly ONE thread is inside the switch below at any
// moment: the one that took `pending` to zero, which cannot happen until the poster has released
// its own reference. An empty wave, or a wave whose tasks all finished before the poster let go,
// is driven onward by this thread in the loop rather than by recursion -- an OCC retry storm would
// otherwise recurse once per restart.
template <bool IofusedPrivateQueue>
ScatterFinish xshard_complete_script(Server& server, ThreadCtx& self, Ring& ring,
                                     const Task& task, Op& op, ScatterState& state) {
    ScatterFinish outcome = ScatterFinish::Waiting;
    bool driving = false;

    // Publishes `next`; returns true when THIS thread still owns the activation afterwards.
    auto launch = [&](ScriptPhase next) -> bool {
        // A queue-full retry re-enters on a synthetic poster task. Clear its marker before making
        // any new owner task visible; otherwise a fast peer can mistake itself for that poster,
        // skip APPLY's owner-sentinel completion, and recursively republish the wave.
        state.script_resume_post = false;
        const ScriptPostResult result = script_post_phase<IofusedPrivateQueue>(
            server, self, ring, task, state, next);
        if (result == ScriptPostResult::Full) {
            // No task slots anywhere. Nothing else references the activation, so the poster's
            // reference simply survives the requeue and the retry resumes this same publication.
            state.script_resume_post = true;
            outcome = ScatterFinish::Retry;
            return false;
        }
        if (result == ScriptPostResult::Empty) return true;   // nothing posted; keep driving
        if (state.pending.fetch_sub(1, std::memory_order_acq_rel) == 1) return true;
        outcome = ScatterFinish::Waiting;
        return false;
    };

    for (;;) {
        if (!driving) {
            if (state.script_resume_post) {
                if (!launch(state.script_phase)) return outcome;
            } else if (state.pending.fetch_sub(1, std::memory_order_acq_rel) != 1) {
                return ScatterFinish::Waiting;
            }
        }
        driving = false;

        switch (state.script_phase) {
            case ScriptPhase::Pin: {
                WorkError error = WorkError::None;
                if (script_group_error(state, error) ||
                    state.aborted.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) {
                    server.note_script_abort_oom();
                    script_engine_error_reply(op, state, error);
                    state.script_apply_after_unpin = false;
                    state.script_commit_after_unpin = false;
                    if (!launch(ScriptPhase::Unpin)) return outcome;
                    driving = true;
                    continue;
                }
                state.script_pins_live = true;
                // All intents now exist. A write before this point is part of the new
                // cut; every write after it is forced through MVCC and can be validated.
                state.script_cut = server.atomic_snapshot();
                state.script_staged_bytes.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
                // TEST HOOK: the park window opens HERE, not at prepare. The point of the
                // hook is to expose the interval between "every declared key is reserved
                // and the cut is chosen" and "the owners actually read", which is the
                // interval AMENDMENT 1 is about.
                if (__builtin_expect(state.debug_script_defer_us != 0, false) &&
                    state.debug_script_defer_deadline == 0)
                    state.debug_script_defer_deadline =
                        now_ns() + static_cast<uint64_t>(state.debug_script_defer_us) * 1000ull;
                if (!launch(ScriptPhase::Read)) return outcome;
                driving = true;
                continue;
            }
            case ScriptPhase::Read: {
                WorkError error = WorkError::None;
                if (script_group_error(state, error) ||
                    state.aborted.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) {
                    server.note_script_abort_oom();
                    script_engine_error_reply(op, state, error);
                    state.script_apply_after_unpin = false;
                    state.script_commit_after_unpin = false;
                    if (!launch(ScriptPhase::Unpin)) return outcome;
                    driving = true;
                    continue;
                }
                if (!launch(ScriptPhase::Run)) return outcome;
                driving = true;
                continue;
            }
            case ScriptPhase::Run:
                if (state.aborted.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) {
                    server.note_script_abort_oom();
                    script_engine_error_reply(op, state, state.final_error);
                    notify_discard_batch(state.notify.exchange(nullptr));
                    state.script_apply_after_unpin = false;
                    state.script_commit_after_unpin = false;
                    if (!launch(ScriptPhase::Unpin)) return outcome;
                    driving = true;
                    continue;
                }
                state.script_has_writes = false;
                for (uint32_t i = 0; i < state.key_count; i++)
                    state.script_has_writes |= (state.status[i] & 2u) != 0;
                // A read-only activation already has a legal serialization point at script_cut: PIN
                // forced every later writer to preserve the predecessor read by STAGE. It therefore
                // needs neither an OCC validation wave nor a commit ticket.
                if (!state.script_has_writes) {
                    server.note_script_activation();
                    state.script_apply_after_unpin = false;
                    state.script_commit_after_unpin = false;
                    if (!launch(ScriptPhase::Unpin)) return outcome;
                    driving = true;
                    continue;
                }
                // Certification through APPLY is deliberately exclusive. Two activations
                // can STAGE and RUN concurrently, but without this seam both can validate
                // the same predecessor before either has installed a candidate, producing a
                // classic lost update. A loser restages instead of parking an executor;
                // plain writers remain fully concurrent and are caught by the ordinary
                // read-set validation below.
                if (!server.script_try_certification()) {
                    if (state.script_retries++ < server.script_crossshard_conflict_retries()) {
                        server.note_script_retry();
                        script_clear_attempt(state, op);
                        state.script_cut = server.atomic_snapshot();
                        if (!launch(ScriptPhase::Read)) return outcome;
                        driving = true;
                        continue;
                    }
                    server.note_script_giveup();
                    op.clear_reply();
                    reply_err(op.sink(), "TRYAGAIN Cross-shard script conflicted, retry");
                    notify_discard_batch(state.notify.exchange(nullptr));
                    state.script_apply_after_unpin = false;
                    state.script_commit_after_unpin = false;
                    if (!launch(ScriptPhase::Unpin)) return outcome;
                    driving = true;
                    continue;
                }
                state.script_certifier = true;
                state.script_ticket = server.atomic_commit_reserve();
                state.script_ticket_live = true;
                state.script_conflict.store(false, std::memory_order_relaxed);
                if (!launch(ScriptPhase::Validate)) return outcome;
                driving = true;
                continue;

            case ScriptPhase::Validate:
                if (state.script_conflict.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) {
                    if (!state.script_ticket_live) std::abort();
                    server.atomic_commit_publish();       // publish the unused reservation
                    state.script_ticket_live = false;
                    if (!state.script_certifier) std::abort();
                    server.script_finish_certification();
                    state.script_certifier = false;
                    if (state.script_retries++ < server.script_crossshard_conflict_retries()) {
                        server.note_script_retry();
                        script_clear_attempt(state, op);
                        state.script_cut = server.atomic_snapshot();
                        if (!launch(ScriptPhase::Read)) return outcome;
                        driving = true;
                        continue;
                    }
                    server.note_script_giveup();
                    op.clear_reply();
                    reply_err(op.sink(), "TRYAGAIN Cross-shard script conflicted, retry");
                    notify_discard_batch(state.notify.exchange(nullptr));
                    state.script_apply_after_unpin = false;
                    state.script_commit_after_unpin = false;
                    if (!launch(ScriptPhase::Unpin)) return outcome;
                    driving = true;
                    continue;
                }
                // Drop the read intents in a separate all-owner wave before installing candidates.
                // The reserved ticket orders every later writer after this activation, and no MVCC
                // record yet points at the group arrays that UNPIN is about to rebuild.
                state.script_apply_after_unpin = true;
                state.script_commit_after_unpin = false;
                if (!launch(ScriptPhase::Unpin)) return outcome;
                driving = true;
                continue;

            case ScriptPhase::Unpin:
                state.script_pins_live = false;
                if (state.script_apply_after_unpin) {
                    state.script_apply_after_unpin = false;
                    if (!launch(ScriptPhase::Apply)) return outcome;
                    driving = true;
                    continue;
                }
                if (state.script_commit_after_unpin) {
                    state.script_commit_after_unpin = false;
                    if (!state.script_ticket_live) std::abort();
                    server.atomic_commit_publish();
                    state.script_ticket_live = false;
                    server.note_script_activation();
                }
                script_snapshot_done(server, state);
                return ScatterFinish::Final;

            case ScriptPhase::Apply: {
                WorkError error = state.final_error;
                const bool failed = script_group_error(state, error) ||
                                    state.aborted.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
                if (failed) {
                    server.note_script_abort_oom();
                    state.aborted.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
                    aof_abort_scatter_group(state);
                    notify_discard_batch(state.notify.exchange(nullptr));
                    if (state.script_ticket_live) {
                        server.atomic_commit_publish();
                        state.script_ticket_live = false;
                    }
                    if (state.script_certifier) {
                        server.script_finish_certification();
                        state.script_certifier = false;
                    }
                    script_engine_error_reply(op, state, error);
                    script_snapshot_done(server, state);
                    return ScatterFinish::Final;
                }
                if (!state.script_ticket_live) std::abort();
                state.epoch.store(state.script_ticket, std::memory_order_release);
                server.atomic_commit_publish();
                state.script_ticket_live = false;
                if (!state.script_certifier) std::abort();
                server.script_finish_certification();
                state.script_certifier = false;
                aof_commit_scatter_group(state, self, ring, state.script_ticket);
                server.note_script_activation();
                server.note_script_group_commit();
                if (__builtin_expect(server.blocking_waiters() != 0, false))
                    blocking_atomic_published(server, self, ring, state);
                script_snapshot_done(server, state);
                return ScatterFinish::Final;
            }
            case ScriptPhase::None:
                std::abort();
        }
        std::abort();
    }
}

template <bool IofusedPrivateQueue>
ScatterFinish xshard_complete_impl(Server& server, ThreadCtx& self, Ring& ring,
                                   const Task& task, Op& op) {
    ScatterState& state = *task.scatter;

            server, self, ring, task, op, state);

        // owner, running on an EX thread. That is the instant the group stops being able to
        // straddle a snapshot cut, and it is much earlier than reply retirement, which happens on
        // the admitting IO thread (the very thread a blocking SAVE occupies).

    }

    FlatStore& store = shard.store();

            const uint32_t pos = state.key_order[group.begin + i];
            if (pos != 1) continue;
            const KeyRef& key = state.keys[pos];
            store.atomic_clear_read_epoch();

        return ScatterTaskResult::Complete;

        state.aborted.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
        return ScatterTaskResult::Complete;
    }

    // and corrupt images pure validation failures, and leaves the normal install loop infallible.
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < group.count; i++) {
        const uint32_t pos = state.key_order[group.begin + i];

    }

    size_t installed_bytes = 0;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < group.count; i++) {
        const uint32_t pos = state.key_order[group.begin + i];

}

    // SAME resize discipline as the ordinary insert() path so the atomic path shares its two hard
    // guarantees: (1) grow at kLoadPct (70%), not at 100% -- a table run to full has no free slot
    // and insert_into would fail; (2) reclaim tombstones. Every atomic detach leaves a tombstone,

    bool atomic_prepare_capacity(uint32_t additional) {

// THERE IS NO UNDO LOG, IN EITHER ATOMIC MODE — AND THAT IS THE SEMANTICS, NOT A GAP.
//
// v1 kept a deep pre-image of every declared key while `--atomic 1` was on and restored it when the
// activation failed (see NOTES-SCRIPTATOMIC.md). Redis has never undone a script's partial effects,
// so an activation that wrote and then raised diverged from the oracle the moment atomics were
// enabled, and the divergence was a LOST WRITE: the restore republished a superseded value over a
// committed one, or erased the key outright when the script had just created it. It also could not
// be made correct in place -- `capture()` read through FlatStore::find(), which resolves at the
// current MVCC read cut, while `rollback()` wrote through the raw erase/insert pair, which does not.
// A read-only activation reads at its pinned program-order cut, so the "original" it captured could
// already be a superseded version — restoring it published a stale value over a newer committed one
// and left any live pending record naming an object the restore had freed.
//
// A script is still externally indivisible: it is one task on one owner, and the single-owner law
// keeps every other task out for its whole duration. Isolation never needed the undo log; only
// failure-atomicity did, and Redis does not offer failure-atomicity.
class ScriptEvictionGuard {
public:
    // Unconditional, so the two atomic modes cannot disagree about what a script observes. Redis
    // does not evict inside an activation either: the OOM decision is taken once, when the script
    // starts. Two plain stores on a cold path; the GET/SET path never reaches here.
    explicit ScriptEvictionGuard(Shard& shard) : store_(&shard.store()) {
        previous_ = store_->script_suspend_eviction();
    }
    ~ScriptEvictionGuard() { store_->script_restore_eviction(previous_); }
    ScriptEvictionGuard(const ScriptEvictionGuard&) = delete;
    ScriptEvictionGuard& operator=(const ScriptEvictionGuard&) = delete;
private:
    FlatStore* store_ = nullptr;
    MaxmemoryPolicy previous_ = MaxmemoryPolicy::NoEviction;
};

struct ScriptContext {
    Shard* shard = nullptr;
    Op* parent = nullptr;
    uint32_t key_first = 0;
    uint32_t key_count = 0;
    uint64_t instructions = 0;
    uint32_t call_index = 0;
    bool timed_out = false;
    uint8_t script_resp = 2;
    // Set per call from the handler variant that entered (clean vs notify registry row). The
    // sandbox closures are built once per persistent state, so notify-variance is a runtime flag
    // here rather than a template parameter — one predictable test per nested call.
    bool notify = false;
    // EVAL_RO / EVALSHA_RO / FCALL_RO, and any function carrying the no-writes flag. Checked at
    // the redis.call dispatch site against the command row's Write bit.
    bool readonly = false;
    // Nested Write-flagged commands that answered without an error: the keyspace effects this
    // activation has already applied and which a failure must NOT reverse.
    uint32_t effect_writes = 0;
    // Filled by the pcall message handler: the first Lua frame's line at the point of the error.
    // Redis reports it in the " ... on @user_script:<line>." tail.
    int error_line = 0;
    uint8_t* cross_access = nullptr;
    uint32_t cross_access_count = 0;
};

// Persistent per-thread engine. Building luaL_newstate + the sandbox + recompiling the source on
// EVERY call measured 53.8k EVALSHA/s at p50 18.9 ms against vanilla redis's 550k/s (~18 µs of
// per-call construction). Scripts execute on shard-owner executors, so one state per thread needs
// no locks: sandbox and compiled chunks are built once; a call rebinds only the context slot and
// the KEYS/ARGV tables. The sandbox closures capture a pointer to `current` (stable for the life
// of the state), never a per-call context address.
struct LuaEngine {
    lua_State* state = nullptr;
    ScriptContext* current = nullptr;   // per-call slot; closures and the hook read through this
    uint64_t flush_generation = 0;      // mirrors g_script_flushes when the state was (re)built
    ~LuaEngine() {
        if (state) lua_close(state);
    }
};
thread_local LuaEngine t_lua_engine;
struct ScriptCrossBinding {
    Op* op = nullptr;
    uint8_t* access = nullptr;
    uint32_t count = 0;
};
thread_local ScriptCrossBinding t_script_cross;
std::atomic<uint64_t> g_script_flushes{0};

ScriptContext* lua_context(lua_State* state) {
    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &g_hook_context_key);
    lua_gettable(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX);
    auto* slot = static_cast<ScriptContext**>(lua_touserdata(state, -1));
    lua_pop(state, 1);
    return slot ? *slot : nullptr;
}

void instruction_hook(lua_State* state, lua_Debug*) {
    ScriptContext* context = lua_context(state);
    if (!context) return;
    context->instructions += kHookInterval;
    if (context->instructions > g_instruction_limit) {
        context->timed_out = true;
        luaL_error(state, "script exceeded the %llu instruction limit",
                   static_cast<unsigned long long>(g_instruction_limit));
    }
}

// pcall message handler. It must not change the error VALUE (Redis distinguishes a raised table
// with an `err` field from a raised string), so it only records where the throw happened: the
// first frame with a real source line, skipping the C frames of redis.call.
int script_error_handler(lua_State* state) {
    ScriptContext* context = lua_context(state);
    if (context) {
        lua_rawseti(state, -2, static_cast<int>(i + 1));
    }
}

void bind_call_globals(lua_State* state, ScriptContext& context) {
    push_call_tables(state, context);
    set_global_raw(state, "ARGV");
    set_global_raw(state, "KEYS");
}

bool append_lua_result(lua_State* state, int index, SmallBuf<kInlineReply>& output,
                       uint32_t depth, uint32_t& elements, std::string& error,
                       bool outer_resp3, uint8_t script_resp) {
    if (depth > kReplyMaxDepth) { error = "script reply nesting is too deep"; return false; }
    index = index < 0 ? lua_gettop(state) + index + 1 : index;
    const int type = lua_type(state, index);
    if (type == LUA_TNIL) {
        reply_null(output, outer_resp3);
        return true;
    }
    if (type == LUA_TBOOLEAN) {
        const bool value = lua_toboolean(state, index);
        if (script_resp == 3) reply_bool(output, value, outer_resp3);
        else if (value) reply_int(output, 1);
        else reply_null(output, outer_resp3);
        return true;
    }
    if (type == LUA_TNUMBER) {
        const lua_Number number = lua_tonumber(state, index);
        if (!std::isfinite(number) || number < static_cast<lua_Number>(LLONG_MIN) ||
            number > static_cast<lua_Number>(LLONG_MAX)) {
            error = "script returned a non-integer number"; return false;
        }
        reply_int(output, static_cast<long long>(number));
        return true;
    }
    if (type == LUA_TSTRING) {
        size_t length = 0;
        const char* value = lua_tolstring(state, index, &length);
        if (length > UINT32_MAX) { error = "script reply is too large"; return false; }
        reply_bulk(output, Slice(value, static_cast<uint32_t>(length)));
        return true;
    }
    if (type != LUA_TTABLE) { reply_null(output, outer_resp3); return true; }

    lua_getfield(state, index, "err");
    if (!lua_isnil(state, -1)) {
        size_t length = 0;
        const char* value = lua_tolstring(state, -1, &length);
        if (!value) { lua_pop(state, 1); error = "invalid redis error table"; return false; }
        output.push_back('-'); output.append(value, length); output.append("\r\n", 2);
        lua_pop(state, 1);
        return true;
    }
    lua_pop(state, 1);
    lua_getfield(state, index, "ok");
    if (!lua_isnil(state, -1)) {
        size_t length = 0;
        const char* value = lua_tolstring(state, -1, &length);
        if (!value) { lua_pop(state, 1); error = "invalid redis status table"; return false; }
        output.push_back('+'); output.append(value, length); output.append("\r\n", 2);
        lua_pop(state, 1);
        return true;
    }
    lua_pop(state, 1);

    lua_getfield(state, index, "double");
    if (lua_isnumber(state, -1)) {
        const double value = static_cast<double>(lua_tonumber(state, -1));
        lua_pop(state, 1);
        reply_double(output, value, outer_resp3);
        return true;
    }
    lua_pop(state, 1);

    lua_getfield(state, index, "big_number");
    if (lua_isstring(state, -1)) {
        size_t length = 0;
        const char* value = lua_tolstring(state, -1, &length);
        std::string safe(value, length);
        for (char& ch : safe) if (ch == '\r' || ch == '\n') ch = ' ';
        lua_pop(state, 1);
        reply_bignum(output, Slice(safe.data(), static_cast<uint32_t>(safe.size())), outer_resp3);
        return true;
    }
    lua_pop(state, 1);

    lua_getfield(state, index, "verbatim_string");
    if (lua_istable(state, -1)) {
        const int verbatim = lua_gettop(state);
        lua_getfield(state, verbatim, "format");
        size_t format_length = 0;
        const char* format = lua_tolstring(state, -1, &format_length);
        lua_getfield(state, verbatim, "string");
        size_t value_length = 0;
        const char* value = lua_tolstring(state, -1, &value_length);
        if (format && format_length >= 3 && value && value_length <= UINT32_MAX) {
            char ext[3] = {format[0], format[1], format[2]};
            reply_verbatim(output, Slice(value, static_cast<uint32_t>(value_length)), ext,
                           outer_resp3);
            lua_pop(state, 3);
            return true;
        }
        lua_pop(state, 2);
    }
    lua_pop(state, 1);

    lua_getfield(state, index, "map");
    if (lua_istable(state, -1)) {
        const int map = lua_gettop(state);
        uint32_t count = 0;
        lua_pushnil(state);
        while (lua_next(state, map)) {
            lua_pop(state, 1);
            if (++count > kReplyMaxElements) {
                error = "script reply has too many elements"; return false;
            }
        }
        reply_map_header(output, count, outer_resp3);
        lua_pushnil(state);
        while (lua_next(state, map)) {
            lua_pushvalue(state, -2);
            if (!append_lua_result(state, -1, output, depth + 1, elements, error,
                                   outer_resp3, script_resp)) return false;
            lua_pop(state, 1);
            lua_pushvalue(state, -1);
            if (!append_lua_result(state, -1, output, depth + 1, elements, error,
                                   outer_resp3, script_resp)) return false;
            lua_pop(state, 2);  // value copy, then original value; retain the iteration key
        }
        lua_pop(state, 1);
        return true;
    }
    lua_pop(state, 1);

    lua_getfield(state, index, "set");
    if (lua_istable(state, -1)) {
        const int set = lua_gettop(state);
        uint32_t count = 0;
        lua_pushnil(state);
        while (lua_next(state, set)) {
            lua_pop(state, 1);
            if (++count > kReplyMaxElements) {
                error = "script reply has too many elements"; return false;
            }
        }
        reply_set_header(output, count, outer_resp3);
        lua_pushnil(state);
        while (lua_next(state, set)) {
            lua_pushvalue(state, -2);
            if (!append_lua_result(state, -1, output, depth + 1, elements, error,
                                   outer_resp3, script_resp)) return false;
            lua_pop(state, 2);  // key copy, then original value; retain the iteration key
        }
        lua_pop(state, 1);
        return true;
    }
    lua_pop(state, 1);

    uint32_t count = 0;
    for (;;) {
        if (++elements > kReplyMaxElements) { error = "script reply has too many elements"; return false; }
        lua_rawgeti(state, index, static_cast<int>(count + 1));
        const bool stop = lua_isnil(state, -1);
        lua_pop(state, 1);
        if (stop) break;
        count++;
    }
    reply_array_header(output, count);
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        lua_rawgeti(state, index, static_cast<int>(i + 1));
        const bool ok = append_lua_result(state, -1, output, depth + 1, elements, error,
                                          outer_resp3, script_resp);
        lua_pop(state, 1);
        if (!ok) return false;
    }
    return true;
}

void script_note_failure(uint32_t effect_writes) {
    if (effect_writes) g_failed_after_effects.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
}

// Builds the wire error for a failed activation, matching Redis 7 byte for byte:
//   <message> script: <tag>, on @<chunk>:<line>.
// A raised table with an `err` field contributes its string unchanged (that is how redis.call and
// error({err=...}) travel); any other raised value is a Lua string that already carries its own
// `user_script:N: ` position prefix and is presented as an ERR.
std::string script_runtime_error(lua_State* state, const ScriptContext& context,
                                 const ScriptInvocation& call) {
    std::string message;
    bool from_table = false;
    if (lua_istable(state, -1)) {
        lua_getfield(state, -1, "err");
        if (lua_isstring(state, -1)) {
            size_t length = 0;
            const char* text = lua_tolstring(state, -1, &length);
            message = clean_error(text, length);
            from_table = true;
        }
        lua_pop(state, 1);
    }
    if (!from_table) {
        size_t length = 0;
        const char* text = lua_tolstring(state, -1, &length);
        message = "ERR " + clean_error(text ? text : "runtime error", text ? length : 13);
    }
    char tail[1024];
    std::snprintf(tail, sizeof(tail), " script: %.*s, on @%s:%d.",
                  static_cast<int>(std::min<uint32_t>(call.tag.n, 512)), call.tag.p, call.chunk,
                  context.error_line > 0 ? context.error_line : 1);
    message += tail;
    return message;
}

}  // namespace

lua_State* script_thread_state() {
    LuaEngine& engine = t_lua_engine;
    if (engine.state &&
        engine.flush_generation != g_script_flushes.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) {
        // SCRIPT FLUSH invalidates every thread's compiled-chunk cache; rebuilding the whole
        // state is the simple correct form and FLUSH is admin-cold. It also drops the FUNCTION
        // library materialization, whose generation stamp lives in the same registry.
        lua_close(engine.state);
        engine.state = nullptr;
        engine.state = nullptr;
    }
    if (!engine.state) {
        engine.state = luaL_newstate();
        if (!engine.state) return nullptr;
        engine.flush_generation = g_script_flushes.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
        create_sandbox_static(engine.state, &engine.current);
        lua_newtable(engine.state);
        lua_setfield(engine.state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX, "tomo_chunks");
        g_state_rebuilds.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    }
    return engine.state;
}

lua_State* script_new_sandbox_state() {
    static ScriptContext* null_slot = nullptr;
    lua_State* state = luaL_newstate();
    if (!state) return nullptr;
    create_sandbox_static(state, &null_slot);
    return state;
}

std::string script_clean_error(const char* text, size_t length) {
    return clean_error(text, length);
}

void script_execute(Shard& shard, Op& op, const ScriptInvocation& call) {
    LuaEngine& engine = t_lua_engine;
    lua_State* state = engine.state;
    ScriptContext context{&shard, &op, call.key_first, call.key_count};
    if (t_script_cross.op == &op) {
        context.cross_access = t_script_cross.access;
        context.cross_access_count = t_script_cross.count;
    }
    context.notify = call.notify;
    context.readonly = call.readonly;
    engine.current = &context;

    ScriptEvictionGuard eviction_guard(shard);

    // The message handler must sit BELOW the callable for lua_pcall; the callable arrived on top.
    lua_pushcfunction(state, script_error_handler);
    lua_insert(state, -2);
    const int handler_index = lua_gettop(state) - 1;
    int arguments = 0;
    if (call.style == ScriptArgStyle::Params) {
        push_call_tables(state, context);
        arguments = 2;
    } else {
        bind_call_globals(state, context);
    }

    lua_sethook(state, instruction_hook, LUA_MASKCOUNT, kHookInterval);
    const int status = lua_pcall(state, arguments, 1, handler_index);
    lua_sethook(state, nullptr, 0, 0);
    if (status != 0) {
        const std::string error = script_runtime_error(state, context, call);
        lua_settop(state, 0);
        engine.current = nullptr;
        // Effects already applied STAND, and the notifications they fired stand with them. Both
        // atomic modes take this same arm, which is what makes the two modes byte-identical to the
        // oracle for a failing activation.
        script_note_failure(context.effect_writes);
        if (context.timed_out) {
            char busy[96];
            std::snprintf(busy, sizeof(busy), "script exceeded the %llu instruction limit",
                          static_cast<unsigned long long>(g_instruction_limit));
            reply_text_error(op, "BUSY", busy);
        } else reply_raw_error(op, error);
        return;
    }

    SmallBuf<kInlineReply> result;
    std::string conversion_error;
    uint32_t elements = 0;
    const bool converted = append_lua_result(
        state, -1, result, 0, elements, conversion_error, op.resp3(), context.script_resp);
    lua_settop(state, 0);
    engine.current = nullptr;
    if (!converted) {
        script_note_failure(context.effect_writes);
        reply_text_error(op, "ERR", std::string("Error running script: ") + conversion_error);
        return;
    }
    op.sink().append(result.data(), result.size());
}

void script_cross_access_begin(Op& op, uint8_t* access, uint32_t count) {
    if (t_script_cross.op) std::abort();
    t_script_cross = ScriptCrossBinding{&op, access, count};
}

void script_cross_access_end() {
    t_script_cross = ScriptCrossBinding{};
}

namespace {

void run_eval(Shard& shard, Op& op, Slice source, bool cache_source, Slice sha_hint,
              bool notify, bool readonly) {
    if (source.n > kScriptMaxBytes) {
        reply_text_error(op, "ERR", "script exceeds the 1 MiB limit");
        return;
    }
    if (source.n && static_cast<uint8_t>(source.p[0]) == 0x1b) {
        reply_text_error(op, "ERR",
                         "Error compiling script (new function): binary chunks are not allowed");
        return;
    }
    uint32_t key_first = 0, key_count = 0;
    if (!command_script_key_range(op, key_first, key_count)) {
            return AddResult::Oom;
        }
        if (!defer_bump) bump();
        return AddResult::Ok;
    }

    mutable std::mutex mu_;
    std::map<std::string, LibraryDef> libraries_;
    std::atomic<uint64_t> generation_{0};
};

FunctionRegistry g_functions;

// ---- the registration sandbox ------------------------------------------------------------------

struct RegisterSink {
    std::vector<FunctionDef>* defs = nullptr;   // metadata harvest (FUNCTION LOAD)
    bool store_callbacks = false;               // materialize into kRegistryFunctions
};

int fn_missing_index(lua_State* state) {
    const char* key = lua_type(state, 2) == LUA_TSTRING ? lua_tostring(state, 2) : "?";
    return luaL_error(state, "Script attempted to access nonexistent global variable '%s'", key);
}

bool field_to_string(lua_State* state, int index, std::string& out) {
    const int type = lua_type(state, index);
    if (type != LUA_TSTRING && type != LUA_TNUMBER) return false;
    size_t length = 0;
    const char* text = lua_tolstring(state, index, &length);
    out.assign(text, length);
bool run_library_body(lua_State* state, Slice code, RegisterSink& sink,
                      bool& compile_failed, std::string& error) {
    compile_failed = false;
    const int base = lua_gettop(state);
    // Lua 5.1 only skips a leading '#' line in luaL_loadfile, never in luaL_loadbuffer, so the
    // shebang has to go before compilation. Blank it IN PLACE (same byte count) rather than
    // slicing it off: every line number Lua reports then matches the source the operator sent,
    // which is what makes "user_function:2:" agree with Redis.
    std::string body;
    try { body.assign(code.p, code.n); }
    catch (const std::bad_alloc&) { error = "ERR out of memory"; return false; }
    for (size_t i = 0; i < body.size() && body[i] != '\n'; i++) body[i] = ' ';
    if (luaL_loadbuffer(state, body.data(), body.size(), kFunctionChunkName) != 0) {
        size_t length = 0;
        const char* text = lua_tolstring(state, -1, &length);
        error = script_clean_error(text ? text : "compile error", text ? length : 13);
        lua_settop(state, base);
        compile_failed = true;
        return false;
    }
    const int chunk = lua_gettop(state);

    get_global_raw(state, "redis");                  // saved real table (or nil)
    const int saved = lua_gettop(state);
    lua_createtable(state, 0, 1);
    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &sink);
    lua_pushcclosure(state, fn_register, 1);
    lua_setfield(state, -2, "register_function");
    lua_createtable(state, 0, 1);
    lua_pushcfunction(state, fn_missing_index);
    lua_setfield(state, -2, "__index");
    lua_setmetatable(state, -2);
    set_global_raw(state, "redis");

    lua_pushvalue(state, chunk);
    const int status = lua_pcall(state, 0, 0, 0);

    lua_pushvalue(state, saved);
    set_global_raw(state, "redis");

    if (status != 0) {
        size_t length = 0;
        std::string message;
        if (lua_istable(state, -1)) {
            lua_getfield(state, -1, "err");
            if (lua_isstring(state, -1)) {
                const char* text = lua_tolstring(state, -1, &length);
                message = script_clean_error(text, length);
            }
            lua_pop(state, 1);
        }
        if (message.empty()) {
            const char* text = lua_tolstring(state, -1, &length);
            message = "ERR " + script_clean_error(text ? text : "runtime error",
                                                  text ? length : 13);
        }
        error = message;
        lua_settop(state, base);
        return false;
    }
    lua_settop(state, base);
    return true;
}

// ---- shebang parsing ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

bool parse_library_header(Slice source, std::string& engine, std::string& name,
                          std::string& error) {
    if (source.n < 2 || source.p[0] != '#' || source.p[1] != '!') {
        error = "Missing library metadata";
        return false;
    }
    return true;
}

// Validates one library source off the executor threads and harvests its registration metadata.
bool compile_library(Slice source, LibraryDef& library, std::string& error) {
    if (source.n > kLibraryMaxBytes) {
        error = "library payload exceeds the 1 MiB limit";
        return false;
    }
    std::string engine;
    if (!parse_library_header(source, engine, library.name, error)) return false;

    lua_State* state = script_new_sandbox_state();
    if (!state) { error = "out of memory"; return false; }
    RegisterSink sink;
    sink.defs = &library.functions;
    bool compile_failed = false;
    std::string body_error;
    const bool ok = run_library_body(state, source, sink, compile_failed, body_error);
    lua_close(state);
    if (!ok) {
        error = compile_failed ? "Error compiling function: " + body_error
                               : "Error registering functions: " + body_error;
        return false;
    }
    if (library.functions.empty()) { error = "No functions registered"; return false; }
    std::sort(library.functions.begin(), library.functions.end(),
              [](const FunctionDef& a, const FunctionDef& b) { return a.name < b.name; });
    try {
        library.code.assign(source.p, source.n);
    } catch (const std::bad_alloc&) {
        error = "out of memory";
        return false;
    }
    return true;
}

// ---- per-thread materialization ------------------------------------------------------------------

// Rebuilds this thread's function table when the registry generation moved. The stamp lives in the
// thread's own Lua registry, so a state that SCRIPT FLUSH rebuilt loses it and re-materializes —
// there is no separate thread_local to keep in step with the interpreter's lifetime.
bool function_thread_sync(lua_State* state, std::string& error) {
    const uint64_t current = g_functions.generation();
    lua_getfield(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX, kRegistryGeneration);
    const bool stamped = lua_isnumber(state, -1);
    const uint64_t loaded = stamped ? static_cast<uint64_t>(lua_tonumber(state, -1)) : 0;
    lua_pop(state, 1);
    if (stamped && loaded == current) return true;

    std::vector<LibraryDef> libraries;
    uint64_t stamp = 0;
    if (!g_functions.snapshot(libraries, stamp)) { error = "out of memory"; return false; }

    lua_newtable(state);
    lua_setfield(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX, kRegistryFunctions);
    RegisterSink sink;
    sink.store_callbacks = true;
    for (const LibraryDef& library : libraries) {
        bool compile_failed = false;
        std::string body_error;
        const Slice code(library.code.data(), static_cast<uint32_t>(library.code.size()));
        if (!run_library_body(state, code, sink, compile_failed, body_error)) {
            // A library that validated at LOAD time failed here: report it rather than serving a
            // half-materialized table, and leave the stamp unset so the next call retries.
            error = "Error materializing library " + library.name + ": " + body_error;
            lua_newtable(state);
            lua_setfield(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX, kRegistryFunctions);
            return false;
        }
    }
    lua_pushnumber(state, static_cast<lua_Number>(stamp));
    lua_setfield(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX, kRegistryGeneration);
    g_thread_rebuilds.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    return true;
}

// ---- FCALL --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// scripting.h — the seam between the Lua interpreter (scripting.cc) and the FUNCTION library
// (functions.cc).
//
// The interpreter is a per-thread singleton owned by scripting.cc: one persistent lua_State per
// executor thread, its sandbox built once, chunks cached by sha in the Lua registry. functions.cc
// owns the process-wide library registry (control-plane state, cold-path mutex) and borrows the
// interpreter through the two calls below. Nothing else crosses: the ScriptContext, the undo log,
// the eviction guard and the reply converter all stay private to scripting.cc.
//
// The Lua amalgamation is compiled exactly once, inside scripting.cc. Other translation units
// include the vendored PUBLIC headers only and link against those definitions.
#pragma once

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <string>

#include "../base/slice.h"

struct lua_State;

namespace tomo {

class Shard;
class Op;

enum class ScriptArgStyle : uint8_t {
    Globals,   // EVAL: KEYS/ARGV are installed as globals; the chunk is called with no arguments.
    Params,    // FCALL: the callback is invoked as callback(keys, args).
};

// One script/function activation. `tag` is the identity Redis prints in its error tail
// ("... script: <tag>, on @<chunk>:<line>."): the sha1 for EVAL, the function name for FCALL.
struct ScriptInvocation {
    uint32_t       key_first = 0;
    uint32_t       key_count = 0;
    ScriptArgStyle style     = ScriptArgStyle::Globals;
    bool           readonly  = false;   // reject Write commands from redis.call/pcall
    bool           notify    = false;   // armed keyspace-notification variant entered
    const char*    chunk     = "user_script";
    Slice          tag;
};

// The calling thread's persistent interpreter, rebuilt when SCRIPT FLUSH moved the generation.
// nullptr on allocation failure. Must be called BEFORE anything is pushed on the returned state:
// a rebuild closes the previous one.
lua_State* script_thread_state();

// A fresh sandboxed state with no context bound — redis.call is present but inert. Used by
// FUNCTION LOAD to validate and to harvest registration metadata off the executor threads. The
// caller owns it and must lua_close() it.
lua_State* script_new_sandbox_state();

// Runs the callable on top of `state` (consumed) under the shard-owner contract: instruction hook,
// atomic undo/rollback, eviction suspension, notification source hooks and RESP conversion. Writes
// the reply — or the Redis-shaped error — into `op`. The stack is left empty either way.
void script_execute(Shard& shard, Op& op, const ScriptInvocation& call);

// Flattens a Lua error string into one RESP-safe line (CR/LF/NUL to spaces, 2 KiB cap).
std::string script_clean_error(const char* text, size_t length);

struct ScriptStats {
    uint64_t cached_scripts    = 0;
    uint64_t compile_hits      = 0;   // per-thread compiled-chunk cache hits
    uint64_t compile_misses    = 0;   // sha compiled into a thread state for the first time
    uint64_t flush_generation  = 0;   // SCRIPT FLUSH count; per-thread states rebuild on change
    uint64_t state_rebuilds    = 0;   // interpreter states constructed (boot + post-FLUSH)
    uint64_t ro_rejections     = 0;   // write commands refused inside a read-only activation
    // Keyspace effects applied from inside activations (nested Write rows that answered without an
    // error), and activations that FAILED with at least one such effect standing. The second is the
    // interleave the removed atomic undo log used to reverse; a test that leaves it at zero has not
    // touched the guarded path.
    uint64_t effect_writes        = 0;
    uint64_t failed_after_effects = 0;
};
ScriptStats script_stats();

struct FunctionStats {
    uint64_t libraries       = 0;
    uint64_t functions       = 0;
    uint64_t generation      = 0;   // LOAD/DELETE/FLUSH/RESTORE count
    uint64_t calls           = 0;   // FCALL/FCALL_RO activations that reached a callback
    uint64_t thread_rebuilds = 0;   // per-thread library re-materializations
    uint64_t ro_rejections   = 0;   // FCALL_RO refused for a function without no-writes
};
FunctionStats function_stats();

// Whether argv[0] of this op is one of the FCALL forms. Routing shares EVAL's numkeys grammar but
// Redis reports a different message for a malformed count.
bool function_is_fcall(const Op& op);

// Cold bridge used by the cross-owner scatter coordinator. Each declared-key byte receives bit 0
// when a nested command reads it and bit 1 when a nested write completes without an error. The
// binding is thread-local and scoped to one outer Op, so ordinary single-owner activations do not
// test or allocate cross-script state.
void script_cross_access_begin(Op& op, uint8_t* access, uint32_t count);
void script_cross_access_end();

}  // namespace tomo
