enum class MultiChildFinish : uint8_t { Waiting, PhaseAdvanced, Final };

void xshard_multi_child_bind(ScatterState& state) {
    // xshard_prepare does not yet know that this state will be driven by an outer EXEC. Undo its
    // standalone phantom pins before publication; child installs retain lazy first-node accounting.
    clear_unpublished_owner_record_refs(state);
    state.multi_child = true;
}

void xshard_multi_child_capture_groups(ScatterState& state,
                                       std::array<uint64_t, 4>& mask) {
    mask.fill(0);
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < state.nsub; i++) {
        const int32_t shard = state.groups[i].shard;
        if (shard < 0 || shard >= 256) std::abort();
        const uint32_t sid = static_cast<uint32_t>(shard);
        mask[sid >> 6] |= 1ull << (sid & 63);
    }
}

bool xshard_multi_child_records_done(const ScatterState& state) {
    return state.record_refs.load(std::memory_order_acquire) == 0 &&
           state.watch_refs.load(std::memory_order_acquire) == 0;
}

MultiChildFinish xshard_multi_child_complete(ScatterState& state, Op& op,
                                             uint32_t owner_thread_id) {
    if (state.atomic_write || (state.atomic_apply && state.phase == 2)) {
        if (!complete_owner_record_wave(state, owner_thread_id))
            return MultiChildFinish::Waiting;
    }
    if (state.pending.fetch_sub(1, std::memory_order_acq_rel) != 1)
        return MultiChildFinish::Waiting;
    if (state.atomic_pop && state.phase == 2 && state.pop_missed) {
        state.final_reply = FinalReply::NullArray;
        return MultiChildFinish::Final;
    }
    if (state.kind == Kind::Sort && state.sort_options.deref && state.phase == 1) {
        if (state.sort_deref->wave == SortDerefWave::Source) {
            WorkError source_error;
            if (first_error(state, source_error)) {
                state.final_reply = FinalReply::Work;
                state.final_error = source_error;
                return MultiChildFinish::Final;
            }
            const WorkError prepared = prepare_sort_deref(state, op);
            if (prepared != WorkError::None) {
                state.final_reply = FinalReply::Work;
                state.final_error = prepared;
                return MultiChildFinish::Final;
            }
            if (sort_deref_gathering(state)) {
                state.pending.store(state.nsub, std::memory_order_release);
                    slot.kind = ValueKind::Nil;
                }
            }
    }
    // RELEASE THE CUT ONLY AFTER THE LAST FRAGMENT HAS ANSWERED. Retirement is that moment: the
    // final reply is assembled once every participating owner has reported, and this is the one
    // retire path a published transaction takes (io_loop.h routes op.has_multi_state() here). The
    // state object is still alive -- multi_retire below is what releases or defers it.
    if (auto* cut = static_cast<MultiExecState*>(op.multi_state())) {
        if (__builtin_expect(cut->snapshot_registered, false))
            loop.scatter_pool_.unregister_snapshot(*loop.srv_, cut, loop.self_->id());
    }
    multi_retire(client, op, loop.multi_deferred_);
    snapshot_bind_io(nullptr, nullptr);
    command_set_local_context(nullptr, nullptr);
}

uint32_t multi_owner_reap_entry(IoLoop& loop) {
    return multi_reap_deferred(loop.multi_deferred_);
}

template <bool IofusedPrivateQueue>
uint32_t multi_owner_pass_entry_impl(IoLoop& loop) {
    uint32_t work = multi_owner_reap_entry(loop);
    while (!loop.pending_multi_cleanups_.empty()) {
        MultiExecState* state = loop.pending_multi_cleanups_.front();
        uint32_t needed[kMaxThreads] = {};
        const uint32_t count = multi_dispatch_count(state);
        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++)
            needed[loop.srv_->worker_of_shard(multi_dispatch_shard(state, i))]++;
        bool room = true;
        for (uint32_t tid = 0; tid < loop.srv_->nthreads(); tid++) {
            if (!needed[tid]) continue;
            ThreadCtx& owner = loop.srv_->thread(tid);
            const uint32_t free_slots = [&] {
                if constexpr (IofusedPrivateQueue)
                    return owner.iofused_task_free_slots(loop.self_->id());
                else
                    return owner.task_free_slots(loop.self_->id());
            }();
            if (free_slots < needed[tid]) {
                room = false;
                break;
            }
        }
        if (!room) break;
        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
            const int32_t sid = multi_dispatch_shard(state, i);
            ThreadCtx& owner = loop.srv_->thread(loop.srv_->worker_of_shard(sid));
            const Task task = multi_make_task(nullptr, UINT64_MAX, sid, state);
            const bool posted = [&] {
                if constexpr (IofusedPrivateQueue)
                    return owner.post_iofused_task(
                        loop.self_->id(), task, loop.ring_, loop.self_->sig());
                else
                    return owner.post_task(
                        loop.self_->id(), task, loop.ring_, loop.self_->sig());
            }();
            if (!posted)
                std::abort();
        }
        multi_internal_dispatch_started(state);
        loop.pending_multi_cleanups_.pop_front();
        work++;
    }
    return work;
}

uint32_t multi_owner_pass_entry(IoLoop& loop) {
    return multi_owner_pass_entry_impl<false>(loop);
}

uint32_t multi_owner_pass_entry_iofused(IoLoop& loop) {
    return multi_owner_pass_entry_impl<true>(loop);
}


int32_t multi_dispatch_shard(const MultiExecState* state, uint32_t index) {
    return state && index < state->shards.size() ? state->shards[index] : -1;
}

void multi_dispatch_started(Client& client, MultiExecState* state) {
    if (!state) return;
    state->published = true;
    MultiSession* session = client.multi_session();
    if (session && session->pending == state) session->pending = nullptr;
}

void multi_internal_dispatch_started(MultiExecState* state) {
    if (state) state->published = true;
}

void multi_abandon_unpublished(MultiExecState* state) {
    if (!state || state->published) return;
    clear_unpublished_multi_record_refs(*state);
    destroy_multi_state(state);
}

bool multi_task_tagged(const Task& task) {
    return (reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(task.scatter) & kMultiTaskTag) != 0;
}

bool multi_task_owns_epoch(const Task& task, const void* group_epoch) {
    const uintptr_t tagged = reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(task.scatter);
    const auto* state = reinterpret_cast<const MultiExecState*>(tagged & ~kMultiTaskTag);
    return state && multi_state_owns_epoch(*state, group_epoch);
}

// INFO atomic_exec_order_late. Defined HERE, outside this file's anonymous namespace, because
// t_server.cc calls it through multi.h: inside, it would be internal-linkage and the reference
// from the other translation unit would not resolve.
uint64_t multi_exec_order_late() { return g_exec_order_late.load(std::memory_order_relaxed); }

Task multi_make_task(Client* client, uint64_t op_id, int32_t shard, MultiExecState* state) {
    const uintptr_t tagged = reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(state) | kMultiTaskTag;
    return Task{client, op_id, shard, reinterpret_cast<ScatterState*>(tagged)};
}

bool multi_aof_emit_fragment(MultiExecState& state, Shard& shard) {
    if (!state.aof_group) return true;
    uint8_t& done = state.aof_shard_done[static_cast<uint32_t>(shard.id())];
    if (done) return true;
    uint32_t count = 0;
    for (const MultiWriteKey& write : state.write_keys) count += write.shard == shard.id();
    if (!count) { done = 1; return true; }
    AofProducer& producer = shard.store().aof();
    if (!producer.begin_group(state.aof_group)) return false;
    // Runtime-error children keep any already-installed candidates private under their own abort
    // word. The physical table head may therefore be a rejected RENAMENX source tombstone. Resolve
    // the transaction's own overlay and record its LOGICAL final image, which skips that child but
    // still sees successful private candidates from the same connection.
    shard.store().atomic_set_read_context(UINT64_MAX, state.origin_conn_id);
    bool ok = true;
    for (const MultiWriteKey& write : state.write_keys) {
        if (write.shard != shard.id()) continue;
        const Slice key(write.key.data(), static_cast<uint32_t>(write.key.size()));
        ok &= producer.record_group_visible_post_image(shard.store(), write.hash, key);
    }
    shard.store().atomic_clear_read_epoch();
    ok &= producer.finish_group();
    done = 1;
    return ok;
}

MultiTaskResult multi_execute_task(Server& server, const Task& task, Shard& shard,
                                   uint32_t owner_thread_id, uint32_t owner_domain,
                                   AofOwnerContext* aof_context) {
    // A carrier-less fragment is not an error: multi_close_entry posts the watch-release fragment
    // of a vanished connection with client=nullptr and op_id=UINT64_MAX, and this function's own
    // tail already destroys the state on that path. Only the notify scope wanted an Op, and a
    // fragment with no client raises no notifications, so it takes the pointer form.
    Op* carrier = task.client && task.op_id != UINT64_MAX
        ? &task.client->rob().at(task.op_id) : nullptr;
    const bool notify = carrier && (carrier->spec->flags & CmdFlags::NotifySelected);
    NotifyExecutionScope notify_scope(shard, carrier, notify);
    const uintptr_t tagged = reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(task.scatter);
    auto& state = *reinterpret_cast<MultiExecState*>(tagged & ~kMultiTaskTag);
    // ONE EXPIRY CUT FOR THE WHOLE TRANSACTION, on every owner and for every fragment including the
    // WATCH phase below -- redis validates watches inside EXEC's own call, under EXEC's snapshot.
    // Without this, two identical reads in one EXEC could disagree about the same key.
    PinnedNowMs now_cut(shard, state.now_cut_ms);
    uint8_t& noted = state.execution_noted[static_cast<uint32_t>(shard.id())];
    if (!(noted & 1u)) {
        shard.note_execution(owner_domain);
        noted |= 1u;
    }
    if (__builtin_expect(atomic_tripwire_enabled(), false) && !(noted & 2u)) {
        multi_tripwire_fragment_begin(state, shard);
        noted |= 2u;
    }
    if (!state.watch_phase_done.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) {
        if (!execute_watch_phase(state, shard)) return MultiTaskResult::Retry;
        if (!state.watch_phase_done.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) return MultiTaskResult::Retry;
    }

    // TEST HOOK (DEBUG ATOMIC-FANOUT-DEFER), the MULTI half. Park every fragment of this
    // transaction except the one on its lead shard until the deadline, so the foreign transaction
    // the battery races really does commit BETWEEN two fragments of one in-EXEC read. It sits
    // AFTER the watch phase deliberately: that phase is an all-participants barrier, so parking
    // ahead of it would hold the lead back too and no fragment would run early. A park, not a
    // stall -- Retry re-queues the task on multi_retries_ and the owner returns to its queue, so
    // the writer is free to execute and publish its ticket inside the window. Off, this is one
    // load of a word the task has already touched.
    if (__builtin_expect(state.debug_fanout_deadline != 0, false) &&
        shard.id() != state.debug_fanout_lead &&
        now_ns() < state.debug_fanout_deadline)
        return MultiTaskResult::Retry;

    const uint32_t shard_id = static_cast<uint32_t>(shard.id());
    std::vector<uint32_t>& command_list = state.shard_commands[shard_id];
    uint32_t& cursor = state.shard_cursors[shard_id];
    if (state.kind != MultiStateKind::Execute ||
            state.keys[i].key_anchor = nullptr;
        }
    }
    state.script_staged_bytes.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    state.script_conflict.store(false, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    notify_discard_batch(state.notify.exchange(nullptr));
}

uint32_t script_select_positions(ScatterState& state, ScriptPhase phase) {
    uint32_t count = 0;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < state.key_count; i++) {
        bool selected = phase == ScriptPhase::Read || phase == ScriptPhase::Unpin;
        if (phase == ScriptPhase::Validate) selected = (state.status[i] & 1u) != 0;
        if (phase == ScriptPhase::Apply) selected = (state.status[i] & 2u) != 0;
        if (selected) state.hop2[count++] = i;
    }
    return count;
}

template <bool IofusedPrivateQueue>
ScriptPostResult script_post_phase(Server& server, ThreadCtx& self, Ring& ring,
                                   const Task& source, ScatterState& state,
                                   ScriptPhase phase) {
    state.script_phase = phase;
    state.phase = phase == ScriptPhase::Apply ? 2 : 1;

    int32_t one_shard = -1;
    if (phase == ScriptPhase::Run) {
        one_shard = state.script_coordinator_shard;
    } else {
        const uint32_t count = script_select_positions(state, phase);
        reset_groups(state);
        build_groups(state, state.hop2, count);
        if (!state.nsub) return ScriptPostResult::Empty;
    }

    uint32_t needed[kMaxThreads] = {};
    uint32_t participants[kMaxThreads];
    uint32_t nparticipants = 0;
    if (phase == ScriptPhase::Run) {
        const uint32_t tid = server.worker_of_shard(one_shard);
        participants[nparticipants++] = tid;
        needed[tid] = 1;
    } else {
        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < state.nsub; i++) {
            const uint32_t tid = server.worker_of_shard(state.groups[i].shard);
            if (needed[tid]++ == 0) participants[nparticipants++] = tid;
        }
    }
    for (uint32_t p = 0; p < nparticipants; p++) {
        const uint32_t tid = participants[p];
        if (scatter_task_free_slots<IofusedPrivateQueue>(
                server.thread(tid), self.id()) < needed[tid])
            return ScriptPostResult::Full;
    }
    if (phase == ScriptPhase::Apply && !state.aof_group &&
        !aof_prepare_scatter_group(state)) {
        state.final_error = WorkError::Oom;
        state.aborted.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
        return ScriptPostResult::Empty;
    }
    // Script starts in phase 1, so xshard_prepare's completion setup deliberately skipped these
    // slots. APPLY is its first and only record-installing wave; construct exactly its owner slots
    // before execute_atomic_apply attaches entries to their `nodes` counters. UNPIN has completed
    // and no record can reference this state yet, so initializing them here cannot reset a live
    // owner count. It is also where APPLY's pre-counted sentinels are published, so it must run
    // exactly once per wave -- the completion count it returns is the same owner count.
    uint32_t task_completions = phase == ScriptPhase::Run ? 1u : state.nsub;
    if (phase == ScriptPhase::Apply)
        task_completions = initialize_owner_completion(state);

    // THE +1 IS THE POSTER'S OWN REFERENCE and it is load-bearing. Owner tasks become visible one
    // participant at a time, so without it the LAST task could finish and try to advance the wave
    // while this thread was still inside the publishing loop -- and the next wave's build_groups()
    // would then rewrite state.groups under a thread already reading it. Two executors inside
    // build_groups() on one arena is exactly how the differ's script leg segfaulted. The poster
    // releases this reference in xshard_complete_script() once publication is complete.
    state.pending.store(task_completions + 1u, std::memory_order_release);
    if (phase == ScriptPhase::Run) {
        ThreadCtx& owner = server.thread(participants[0]);
        const Task post{source.client, source.op_id, one_shard, &state};
        if (!scatter_post_task_quiet<IofusedPrivateQueue>(
                owner, self.id(), post, self.sig())) std::abort();
        owner.flush_task_notify(self.id(), ring, self.sig());
        return ScriptPostResult::Posted;
    }

    Task posts[256];
    uint16_t begin[kMaxThreads];
    uint32_t cursor = 0;
    for (uint32_t p = 0; p < nparticipants; p++) {
        begin[p] = static_cast<uint16_t>(cursor);
        cursor += needed[participants[p]];
        needed[participants[p]] = begin[p];
    }
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < state.nsub; i++) {
        const uint32_t tid = server.worker_of_shard(state.groups[i].shard);
        posts[needed[tid]++] = Task{source.client, source.op_id, state.groups[i].shard, &state};
    }
    for (uint32_t p = 0; p < nparticipants; p++) {
        const uint32_t tid = participants[p];
        const uint32_t end = p + 1 < nparticipants ? begin[p + 1] : cursor;
        ThreadCtx& owner = server.thread(tid);
        if (!scatter_post_tasks_quiet<IofusedPrivateQueue>(
                owner, self.id(), posts + begin[p], end - begin[p], self.sig()))
            std::abort();

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Shared client, geometry and reporting helpers for tests/*.py.

`import _lib` works from any battery because python3 puts the script's own directory (tests/)
first on sys.path. Nothing here opens a server; every helper takes a live connection.

House rules this module encodes (they are rules, not preferences -- see AUDIT-TESTS.md):

  * DETERMINISTIC hooks over timing luck. `armed()` arms a DEBUG window hook and ALWAYS disarms
    it, and refuses to proceed if the arm did not answer OK (an unarmed "deterministic" arm is a
    timing arm in disguise).
  * A geometry claim is PROVED on this boot. `shard_of()` and `topology()` ask the server; nothing
    is inferred from key names or from the default shard-home map (the hash seed is drawn from the
    kernel at every boot, and the balancer can move shards).
  * "Owner" means the thread that owns a shard -- the `shard <sid> <owner_tid>` rows of DEBUG
    LBSIGNALS -- never the `ex` role label. Under --thread-mode 1s every thread is labelled `fused`;
    ownership still comes from shard rows. Every helper here behaves identically in 1s and 2s.
  * A skip is visible and carries a reason. `Report.skip(..., strict=True)` marks a skip that
    means "the mechanism could not be armed" (a DEBUG hook denied, a knob absent); under
    TOMO_GATE_STRICT=1 -- exported by tests/gate.sh -- such a skip fails the battery, so a gate row
    can never turn green by silently skipping the arm it exists for. A probabilistic discovery arm
    that found no window is `strict=False`: it is reported, never a failure.
  * `skip_all(reason)` exits 3 when a whole battery cannot apply to this boot (a 2s-only feature on
    a 1s boot). The gate's `py()` wrapper paints exit 3 red: a row that cannot run is a gate
    defect, not a pass.
"""

import contextlib
import os
import socket
import sys
import time
from collections import namedtuple

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# RESP client
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


class RespError(Exception):
    """A `-ERR ...` reply. Returned by Conn.read(), never raised by it, so a reader thread keeps
    the server's exact text instead of a generic exception."""

    def __init__(self, message):
        if isinstance(message, str):
            message = message.encode()
        super().__init__(message)
        self.message = message

    def __eq__(self, other):
        return isinstance(other, RespError) and self.message == other.message

    def __hash__(self):
        return hash(self.message)

    def __repr__(self):
        return "RespError(%r)" % self.message

    def __str__(self):
        return self.message.decode("utf-8", "replace")


def encode(*args):
    """One RESP command frame. str -> utf-8, bytes as-is, everything else via str()."""
    parts = [b"*%d\r\n" % len(args)]
    for arg in args:
        if isinstance(arg, str):
            arg = arg.encode()
        elif not isinstance(arg, (bytes, bytearray)):
            arg = str(arg).encode()
        parts.append(b"$%d\r\n%s\r\n" % (len(arg), arg))
    return b"".join(parts)


class Conn:
    """A blocking RESP2/RESP3 connection with a complete reader.

    read() returns: simple strings and verbatim/bulk strings as bytes, integers as int, nulls as
    None, arrays/sets/pushes as lists, maps as FLAT [k, v, k, v] lists (order preserved, duplicate
    keys kept), doubles/big numbers/booleans as their raw bytes (`,1.5` -> b"1.5", `#t` -> b"t"),
    attributes (`|`) are consumed and discarded, and errors as RespError instances.
    """

    def __init__(self, host, port, timeout=30.0, nodelay=True, rcvbuf=None, buffering=1 << 20):
        self.host, self.port = host, int(port)
        self.sock = socket.create_connection((host, int(port)), timeout=timeout)
        self.sock.settimeout(timeout)
        if nodelay:
            self.sock.setsockopt(socket.IPPROTO_TCP, socket.TCP_NODELAY, 1)
        if rcvbuf:
            self.sock.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_RCVBUF, rcvbuf)
            if hasattr(socket, "TCP_WINDOW_CLAMP"):
                self.sock.setsockopt(socket.IPPROTO_TCP, socket.TCP_WINDOW_CLAMP, rcvbuf)
        self.file = self.sock.makefile("rb", buffering=buffering)

    # -- transport ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def raw(self, payload):
        self.sock.sendall(payload)

    def send(self, *args):
        self.sock.sendall(encode(*args))

    def close(self, reset=False):
        if self.sock is None:
            return
        try:
            if reset:
                import struct
                self.sock.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_LINGER, struct.pack("ii", 1, 0))
            self.file.close()
            self.sock.close()
        except OSError:
            pass
        self.sock = None

    # -- reader ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _line(self):
        line = self.file.readline()
        if not line:
            raise EOFError("server closed the connection")

bool execute_watch_phase(MultiExecState& state, Shard& shard) {
    if (state.watch_shard_done[static_cast<uint32_t>(shard.id())]) return true;
    if (state.kind == MultiStateKind::WatchAdd) {
        for (const MultiWatchedKey& watched : state.watched) {
            if (watched.shard != shard.id()) continue;
            const Slice key(watched.key.data(), static_cast<uint32_t>(watched.key.size()));
            if (!shard.watch_add(key, state.client, state.watch_generation)) return false;
        }
    } else if (state.kind == MultiStateKind::Execute) {
        for (const MultiWatchedKey& watched : state.watched) {
            if (watched.shard != shard.id()) continue;
            const Slice key(watched.key.data(), static_cast<uint32_t>(watched.key.size()));
            if (!shard.watch_validate_and_reserve(
                    key, state.client, state.watch_generation, &state, &state.epoch,
                    &state.aborted, &state.watch_refs,
                    state_writes_key(state, watched))) return false;
        }
        if (state.client->watch_dirty()) {
            state.watch_failed.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
            state.aborted.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
        }
        for (const MultiWatchedKey& watched : state.watched) {
            if (watched.shard != shard.id()) continue;
            shard.watch_remove(Slice(watched.key.data(), static_cast<uint32_t>(watched.key.size())),
                               state.client, state.watch_generation);
        }
    } else {
        for (const MultiWatchedKey& watched : state.watched) {
            if (watched.shard != shard.id()) continue;
            // A prior atomic writer may have completed its owner pass while its global decision is
            // still unpublished.  Keep UNWATCH/DISCARD/close behind that decision so removing the
            // last watcher also releases the reservation's state-lifetime pin.
            if (!shard.watch_write_ready(
                    Slice(watched.key.data(), static_cast<uint32_t>(watched.key.size()))))
                return false;
            shard.watch_remove(Slice(watched.key.data(), static_cast<uint32_t>(watched.key.size())),
                               state.client, state.watch_generation);
        }
    }
    state.watch_shard_done[static_cast<uint32_t>(shard.id())] = 1;
    if (state.watch_pending.fetch_sub(1, std::memory_order_acq_rel) == 1)
        state.watch_phase_done.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
    return true;
}

void finalize_reservations(MultiExecState& state, Shard& shard) {
    if (state.final_shard_done[static_cast<uint32_t>(shard.id())]) return;
    for (const MultiWatchedKey& watched : state.watched) {
        if (watched.shard != shard.id()) continue;
        shard.watch_write_ready(
            Slice(watched.key.data(), static_cast<uint32_t>(watched.key.size())), nullptr);
    }
    for (const MultiWriteKey& write : state.write_keys) {
        if (write.shard != shard.id()) continue;
        shard.watch_write_ready(
            Slice(write.key.data(), static_cast<uint32_t>(write.key.size())), nullptr);
    }
    state.final_shard_done[static_cast<uint32_t>(shard.id())] = 1;
    }
    set_state_reply(*state, op);
    op.detach_scatter_state();
    client.atomic_group_finished();
    if (state->reset_watch) {
        client.next_watch_generation();
        client.clear_watch_dirty();
    }
    release_admission(*state);
    state->retired = true;
    if (multi_records_done(*state)) {
        destroy_multi_state(state);
        return;
    }
    try { deferred.push_back(state); }
    catch (const std::bad_alloc&) {
        // The record refs keep the state valid.  An allocation failure leaks one transaction state
        // rather than freeing epoch/abort words still named by shard-local MVCC entries.
    }
}

uint32_t multi_reap_deferred(std::vector<MultiExecState*>& deferred) {
    uint32_t reaped = 0;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < deferred.size();) {
        MultiExecState* state = deferred[i];
        if (!multi_records_done(*state)) { i++; continue; }
        destroy_multi_state(state);
        deferred[i] = deferred.back();
        deferred.pop_back();
        reaped++;
    }
    return reaped;
}

MultiExecState* multi_prepare_close(Server& server, Client& client, uint32_t owner_io) {
    MultiSession* session = client.multi_session();
    if (!session) return nullptr;
    if (session->pending && !session->pending->published) {
        MultiExecState* pending = session->pending;
        session->pending = nullptr;
        multi_abandon_unpublished(pending);
    }
    session->active = false;
    session->queue_error = false;
    session->queue.clear();
    if (session->watched.empty()) return nullptr;
    MultiExecState* state = prepare_unwatch_state(
        server, client, owner_io, *session, MultiStateKind::Close, MultiFinalReply::Ok);
    return state;
}

void multi_session_destroy(MultiSession* session) {
    if (!session) return;
    if (session->pending && !session->pending->published)
        multi_abandon_unpublished(session->pending);
    delete session;
}

bool multi_session_active(const Client& client) {
    const MultiSession* session = client.multi_session();
    return session && session->active;
}

uint32_t multi_session_queue_size(const Client& client) {
    const MultiSession* session = client.multi_session();
    return session && session->active ? static_cast<uint32_t>(session->queue.size()) : 0;
}

    NotHandled,
    LocalDone,
    Dispatch,
    Backpressure,
};

enum class MultiTaskResult : uint8_t {
    Retry,
    Complete,
    Final,
};

// Called after lookup/arity validation.  Transaction controls are handled here; while MULTI is
// active every other accepted command is copied into connection-lived storage and answered QUEUED.
MultiIoAction multi_handle_io(Server& server, Client& client, Op& op, uint32_t owner_io,
                              MultiExecState*& dispatch);
bool multi_queueing(const Client& client);
void multi_mark_queue_error(Client& client);

// The IO loop deliberately contains only predicted-cold calls into these entries.  Keeping the
// transaction dispatch and lifetime machinery in multi.inc preserves the layout of the ordinary
// parse/dispatch and retirement paths.
bool multi_dispatch_entry(IoLoop& loop, Client& client, Op& op, uint32_t consumed);
bool multi_dispatch_entry_iofused(IoLoop& loop, Client& client, Op& op, uint32_t consumed);
void multi_retire_entry(IoLoop& loop, Client& client, Op& op);
uint32_t multi_owner_pass_entry(IoLoop& loop);
uint32_t multi_owner_pass_entry_iofused(IoLoop& loop);
uint32_t multi_owner_reap_entry(IoLoop& loop);
void multi_close_entry(IoLoop& loop, Client& client);
void multi_shutdown_entry(IoLoop& loop);

uint32_t multi_dispatch_count(const MultiExecState* state);
int32_t multi_dispatch_shard(const MultiExecState* state, uint32_t index);
void multi_dispatch_started(Client& client, MultiExecState* state);
void multi_internal_dispatch_started(MultiExecState* state);
void multi_abandon_unpublished(MultiExecState* state);

// Low-bit tagging reuses Task::scatter without changing the 32-byte queue item.
bool multi_task_tagged(const Task& task);
// Does `group_epoch` belong to this fragment's OWN logical unit? The transaction's plain per-key
// installs publish through its own epoch word; every cross-shard command lowered inside the same
// EXEC keeps its own ScatterState and publishes through that one. A caller asking "is there an
// undecided record here that is not mine" has to accept both, or a transaction holds against its
// own child (NOTES-MULTIRES.md §5(a)).
bool multi_task_owns_epoch(const Task& task, const void* group_epoch);
// INFO atomic_exec_order_late: times an EXEC write reached its install with an undecided record
// from another logical unit of the same connection still on this owner -- the ordering violation
// the dispatch-time park in ExLoop::execute() exists to make impossible. It is a BUG counter and
// must read zero; it is separate from atomic_exec_order_holds precisely so that "the hold fired"
// and "the hold fired too late" cannot be confused for one another (NOTES-MULTIRACE.md §5).
uint64_t multi_exec_order_late();
Task multi_make_task(Client* client, uint64_t op_id, int32_t shard, MultiExecState* state);
MultiTaskResult multi_execute_task(Server& server, const Task& task, Shard& shard,
                                   uint32_t owner_thread_id, uint32_t owner_domain,
                                   AofOwnerContext* aof_context);

// IO-side retirement owns state destruction.  Pending MVCC records may retain the shared epoch
// after the EXEC reply, so those states are reaped when their owner-local record refs reach zero.
void multi_retire(Client& client, Op& op, std::vector<MultiExecState*>& deferred);
uint32_t multi_reap_deferred(std::vector<MultiExecState*>& deferred);

// Connection teardown.  A watched connection stays alive until owner tasks remove every registry
// entry; the returned state is dispatched exactly like an internal MULTI task (op_id == UINT64_MAX).
MultiExecState* multi_prepare_close(Server& server, Client& client, uint32_t owner_io);
void multi_session_destroy(MultiSession* session);
bool multi_session_active(const Client& client);
uint32_t multi_session_queue_size(const Client& client);
uint32_t multi_session_watch_size(const Client& client);
uint64_t multi_session_memory(const Client& client);

// Ordinary owner-local write hook.  The false result means an EXEC still holds a WATCH validation
// reservation on one of this command's keys and the task must be retried, not executed early.
bool multi_plain_write_ready(Shard& shard, Op& op);
void multi_plain_write_committed(Shard& shard, Op& op);

}  // namespace tomo

ScriptContext* lua_context(lua_State* state) {
    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &g_hook_context_key);
    lua_gettable(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX);
    auto* slot = static_cast<ScriptContext**>(lua_touserdata(state, -1));
    lua_pop(state, 1);
    return slot ? *slot : nullptr;
}

void instruction_hook(lua_State* state, lua_Debug*) {
    ScriptContext* context = lua_context(state);
    if (!context) return;
    context->instructions += kHookInterval;
    if (context->instructions > g_instruction_limit) {
        context->timed_out = true;
        luaL_error(state, "script exceeded the %llu instruction limit",
                   static_cast<unsigned long long>(g_instruction_limit));
    }

        live_config_version_.store(2, std::memory_order_release);  // even versions are stable
        unix_owner_tid_ = cfg.unixsocket && *cfg.unixsocket
            ? placement_.ifid_threads().front() : UINT32_MAX;
        if (!adjust_open_files_limit()) return false;
        check_tcp_backlog_settings();
        // Shard maps are resolved exactly once at boot; parsing never leaks onto a request path.
        if (!placement_.assign_shard_homes(cfg.shards)) return false;

        // ---- shards: bucket ranges, fixed for the life of the process ----------------------------
        shards_.resize(cfg.shards);
        const uint32_t per = kNumBuckets / cfg.shards;
        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < cfg.shards; i++) {
            const uint32_t b0 = i * per;
            const uint32_t b1 = (i + 1 == cfg.shards) ? kNumBuckets : (i + 1) * per;
            shards_[i] = std::make_unique<Shard>();
            shards_[i]->init(this, static_cast<int32_t>(i), b0, b1, cfg.zc_min, cfg.type_limits,
                             cfg.stream_limits);
            if (key_lb_signals_enabled() && !shards_[i]->enable_lb_signals()) {
                std::fprintf(stderr, "fatal: could not allocate weighted-placement signals\n");
                return false;
            }
            shards_[i]->bind_atomic_state(
                [](void* ctx) { return static_cast<Server*>(ctx)->atomic_commit(); }, this,
                &atomic_activity_, &script_intent_owners_);
        }
        router_.build_uniform(static_cast<int32_t>(cfg.shards));

        // ---- threads ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
        // Every front-end has already lowered to dense per-thread entries. Every thread still gets
        // a producer lane from every other, because a role change must not require re-wiring
        // the mesh; the TASK lanes are a role-partitioned masked monolith whose block sizes are
        // re-derived at each role change (ThreadCtx::remask_quiesced), while the client, release
        // and transfer channels stay uniform per-thread arrays.
        const uint32_t nthreads = placement_.total_threads();
public:
    Shard() = default;
    ~Shard();
    Shard(const Shard&) = delete;
    Shard& operator=(const Shard&) = delete;

    void init(Server* server, int32_t id, uint32_t bucket_begin, uint32_t bucket_end, uint32_t zc_min,
              const TypeLimits& type_limits, const StreamLimits& stream_limits) {
        server_ = server;
        id_ = id;
        bucket_begin_ = bucket_begin;
        bucket_end_   = bucket_end;
        zc_min_ = zc_min;
        type_limits_ = type_limits;
        stream_limits_ = stream_limits;
        store_.bind_expired_counter(&stats_.expired);
        store_.bind_evicted_counter(&stats_.evicted);
        store_.bind_rehash_counter(&stats_.rehashes);
        flat_notify_sink_.context = this;
        flat_notify_sink_.enabled = notify_flat_enabled;
        flat_notify_sink_.emit = notify_flat_emit;
        notify_bind_flat_store(&store_, &flat_notify_sink_);
    }

    // A cross-owner script executes against a private, executor-thread-local workbench. It owns
    // every routing bucket logically, borrows nothing, and deliberately does not join the global
    // notification binding list or bind AOF/MVCC/maxmemory state. Nested notify-aware handlers pass
    // this sink explicitly, so the normal event builder still sees their exact command sequence.
    void init_private(Server* server, int32_t id, const TypeLimits& type_limits,
                      const StreamLimits& stream_limits) {
        server_ = server;
        id_ = id;
        bucket_begin_ = 0;
        bucket_end_ = kNumBuckets;
        zc_min_ = UINT32_MAX;
        type_limits_ = type_limits;
        stream_limits_ = stream_limits;
        store_.bind_expired_counter(&stats_.expired);
        store_.bind_evicted_counter(&stats_.evicted);
        flat_notify_sink_.context = this;
        flat_notify_sink_.enabled = notify_flat_enabled;
        flat_notify_sink_.emit = notify_flat_emit;
    }

    int32_t  id() const { return id_; }
    bool     owns(uint32_t bucket) const { return bucket >= bucket_begin_ && bucket < bucket_end_; }
    uint32_t bucket_begin() const { return bucket_begin_; }
    uint32_t bucket_end()   const { return bucket_end_; }
    uint32_t zc_min()       const { return zc_min_; }
    void set_zc_min(uint32_t value) { zc_min_ = value; }
    int64_t  now_ms()       const { return now_ms_; }
    const TypeLimits& type_limits() const { return type_limits_; }
    void set_type_limits(const TypeLimits& value) { type_limits_ = value; }

port_listeners(){ # pids bound to a port, listening or not yet accepting (ss names the owner)
  ss -H -ltnp "sport = :$1" 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.*pid=\([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p' | sort -u \
      | paste -sd, -
}
guard_port(){ # a bound listener OR an accepting peer on the port ends the gate, naming the pid
  local owners; owners=$(port_listeners "$1")
  if [ -n "$owners" ] || (exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/$1) 2>/dev/null; then
    say "port $1 pre-boot guard" \
        "FAIL (already listening${owners:+; pid=$owners} -- a leftover server; kill it and re-run)"
    exit 1
  fi
}
settle(){ # after a server is gone: wait for $PORT to stop accepting, then a short settle.
  # Replaces a fixed `sleep 5` (x55 per run, ~4.6 min). Not load-bearing: the listener sets
  # SO_REUSEADDR+SO_REUSEPORT (src/core/io_loop.h:167) and `wait` already reaped the process.
  # GATE_STOP_SETTLE=5 restores the old timing if a row ever turns out to depend on it -- which
  # would itself be a finding worth a NOTES line.
  for _ in $(seq 50); do (exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/$PORT) 2>/dev/null || break; sleep 0.1; done
  sleep "${GATE_STOP_SETTLE:-1}"
}
launch(){ # logtag binary args... -> pid in $SRV, log in $SRVLOG; waits up to 30 s for the port
  local tag=$1 bin=$2; shift 2
  quiet_wait
  SRV=0; SRVLOG=/dev/null
  guard_port "$PORT"
  [ -x "$bin" ] || { say "boot ($tag)" "FAIL ($bin is not an executable)"; return 1; }
  SRVLOG=$(mktemp "/tmp/gate-srv-$tag.XXXXXX")
  taskset -c $CORES "$bin" --port $PORT --bind 127.0.0.1 --shards 16 "$@" > "$SRVLOG" 2>&1 &
  SRV=$!
  # 30s, not 10s: the AOF replay boot replays its file BEFORE it listens, and on a box shared
  # with other lanes that overran a 10s deadline and turned six AOF rows red with no defect behind
  # them. A generous deadline costs nothing when the server is quick — the loop exits on connect.
  for _ in $(seq 150); do
    if ! kill -0 "$SRV" 2>/dev/null; then
      wait "$SRV" 2>/dev/null; boot_log_tail "$tag" "exited before it listened"; return 1
    fi
    (exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/$PORT) 2>/dev/null && return 0; sleep 0.2; done
  boot_log_tail "$tag" "never accepted on $PORT within 30s"
  return 1
}
boot_log_tail(){ # a boot that failed is a defect report, not a filename: SHOW the server's words.
                 # Tonight three boot failures were triaged twice over because the row said only
                 # "see $SRVLOG" and the log was rotated by the next row's mktemp before anyone
                 # opened it.
  printf 'GATE: boot (%s) %s -- last 25 lines of %s:\n' "$1" "$2" "$SRVLOG" >&2
  tail -n 25 "$SRVLOG" 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/GATE|   /' >&2
}
boot(){ local bin=$1; shift; launch main "$bin" --ratio $GATE_RATIO "$@"; }
boot_fused(){ # deliberately omits --ratio, which fused mode rejects
  local bin=$1; shift; launch fused "$bin" --thread-mode fused "$@"; }
stop(){ kill -TERM $SRV 2>/dev/null; wait $SRV 2>/dev/null; settle; }
shutdown_clean(){ python3 tests/shutdown_report.py "$SRVLOG" clean; }
shutdown_present(){ python3 tests/shutdown_report.py "$SRVLOG" present; }
shutdown_value(){ python3 tests/shutdown_report.py "$SRVLOG" get "$1"; }

+int script_pcall_library(lua_State* state) {
+    ScriptContext context;
+    ScriptContext* current = &context;
+    // Keep the previous context slot rooted below the callable while the library runs. This
+    // works for both the temporary LOAD interpreter and an executor's persistent interpreter.
+    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &g_hook_context_key);
+    lua_rawget(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX);
+    lua_insert(state, -2);
+    const int saved = lua_gettop(state) - 1;
+    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &g_hook_context_key);
+    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &current);
+    lua_rawset(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX);
+    lua_sethook(state, instruction_hook, LUA_MASKCOUNT, kHookInterval);
+    int status = lua_pcall(state, 0, 0, 0);
+    lua_sethook(state, nullptr, 0, 0);
+    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &g_hook_context_key);
+    lua_pushvalue(state, saved);
+    lua_rawset(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX);
+    lua_remove(state, saved);
+    if (context.timed_out) {
+        if (status != 0) lua_pop(state, 1);
+        lua_pushliteral(state, "ERR function library exceeded the instruction limit");
+        status = LUA_ERRRUN;
+    }
+    return status;
+}

uint32_t multi_owner_pass_entry(IoLoop& loop) {
    return multi_owner_pass_entry_impl<false>(loop);
}

uint32_t multi_owner_pass_entry_iofused(IoLoop& loop) {
    return multi_owner_pass_entry_impl<true>(loop);
}

void multi_close_entry(IoLoop& loop, Client& client) {
    if (MultiExecState* cleanup = multi_prepare_close(*loop.srv_, client, loop.self_->id()))
        loop.pending_multi_cleanups_.push_back(cleanup);
}

+int script_pcall_library(lua_State* state) {
+    ScriptContext context;
+    ScriptContext* current = &context;
+    // Keep the previous context slot rooted below the callable while the library runs. This
+    // works for both the temporary LOAD interpreter and an executor's persistent interpreter.

+    lua_insert(state, -2);

+    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &g_hook_context_key);
+    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &current);
+    lua_rawset(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX);
+    lua_sethook(state, instruction_hook, LUA_MASKCOUNT, kHookInterval);
+    int status = lua_pcall(state, 0, 0, 0);
+    lua_sethook(state, nullptr, 0, 0);
+    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &g_hook_context_key);
+    lua_pushvalue(state, saved);
+    lua_rawset(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX);
+    lua_remove(state, saved);
+    if (context.timed_out) {
+        if (status != 0) lua_pop(state, 1);
+        lua_pushliteral(state, "ERR function library exceeded the instruction limit");
+        status = LUA_ERRRUN;
+    }
+    return status;

+    lua_pushvalue(state, saved);
+    lua_rawset(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX);

+        if (status != 0) lua_pop(state, 1);
+        lua_pushliteral(state, "ERR function library exceeded the instruction limit");
+        status = LUA_ERRRUN;
+    }
+    return status;

+int script_pcall_library(lua_State* state) {
+    ScriptContext context;
+    ScriptContext* current = &context;
+    // Keep the previous context slot rooted below the callable while the library runs. This
+    // works for both the temporary LOAD interpreter and an executor's persistent interpreter.
+    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &g_hook_context_key);
+    lua_rawget(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX);
+    lua_insert(state, -2);
+    const int saved = lua_gettop(state) - 1;
+    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &g_hook_context_key);
+    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &current);
+    lua_rawset(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX);
+    lua_sethook(state, instruction_hook, LUA_MASKCOUNT, kHookInterval);
+    int status = lua_pcall(state, 0, 0, 0);
+    lua_sethook(state, nullptr, 0, 0);
+    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &g_hook_context_key);
+    lua_pushvalue(state, saved);
+    lua_rawset(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX);
+    lua_remove(state, saved);
+    if (context.timed_out) {
+        if (status != 0) lua_pop(state, 1);
+        lua_pushliteral(state, "ERR function library exceeded the instruction limit");
+        status = LUA_ERRRUN;
+    }
+    return status;
+}

+int script_pcall_library(lua_State* state) {
+    ScriptContext context;
+    ScriptContext* current = &context;
+    // Keep the previous context slot rooted below the callable while the library runs. This
+    // works for both the temporary LOAD interpreter and an executor's persistent interpreter.

+    lua_insert(state, -2);

+    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &current);
+    lua_rawset(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX);
+    lua_sethook(state, instruction_hook, LUA_MASKCOUNT, kHookInterval);
+    int status = lua_pcall(state, 0, 0, 0);
+    lua_sethook(state, nullptr, 0, 0);
+    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &g_hook_context_key);
+    lua_pushvalue(state, saved);
+    lua_rawset(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX);
+    lua_remove(state, saved);
+    if (context.timed_out) {
+        if (status != 0) lua_pop(state, 1);
+        lua_pushliteral(state, "ERR function library exceeded the instruction limit");
+        status = LUA_ERRRUN;
+    }
+    return status;

+int script_pcall_library(lua_State* state) {
+    ScriptContext context;
+    ScriptContext* current = &context;
+    // Keep the previous context slot rooted below the callable while the library runs. This
+    // works for both the temporary LOAD interpreter and an executor's persistent interpreter.

+    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &current);
+    lua_rawset(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX);
+    lua_sethook(state, instruction_hook, LUA_MASKCOUNT, kHookInterval);
+    int status = lua_pcall(state, 0, 0, 0);
+    lua_sethook(state, nullptr, 0, 0);
+    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &g_hook_context_key);
+    lua_pushvalue(state, saved);
+    lua_rawset(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX);
+    lua_remove(state, saved);
+    if (context.timed_out) {
+        if (status != 0) lua_pop(state, 1);
+        lua_pushliteral(state, "ERR function library exceeded the instruction limit");
+        status = LUA_ERRRUN;
+    }
+    return status;

 // Runs the callable on top of `state` (consumed) under the shard-owner contract: instruction hook,

codex
The script write window needs two protections: retain each write intent until its owner installs the image, and check again immediately before installation. That lets ordinary writes proceed while making the stale script return `TRYAGAIN`. I’m adding deterministic tests that drive the owner phases directly, so this check won’t depend on winning a timing race.
apply patch

+int script_pcall_library(lua_State* state) {

+    lua_pushvalue(state, saved);
+    lua_rawset(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX);
+    lua_remove(state, saved);

+        status = LUA_ERRRUN;
+    }

public:
    static constexpr uint64_t kAtomicEnabledBit = uint64_t{1} << 63;

    Server() = default;
    Server(const Server&) = delete;
    Server& operator=(const Server&) = delete;

    // Resolve placement and the shard default once, before AOF/snapshot recovery reads geometry.
    bool prepare_boot(Config& cfg) {
        const char* domains = std::getenv("TOMOKV_L3_DOMAINS");
        if (domains && *domains) {
            if (!topo_.declare(domains)) {
                std::fprintf(stderr, "fatal: TOMOKV_L3_DOMAINS '%s' invalid\n", domains);
                return false;
            }
        } else if (!topo_.discover()) {
            std::fprintf(stderr, "fatal: could not discover any allowed cpu\n");
            return false;
        }
        if (!topo_.discover_thread_siblings()) {
            std::fprintf(stderr, "fatal: could not read Linux thread_siblings_list topology\n");
            return false;
        }
        smt_mode_ = topo_.allowed_sibling_pairs() != 0;
        bool placed = false;
        if (cfg.thread_mode == ThreadMode::Fused) {
            placed = placement_.build_fused(topo_, cfg.place);
        } else {
            // Default shape: an even io/ex split of every allowed cpu, io taking the odd one out --
            // the measured 2s center (4:4-class) generalized to any core count.
            uint32_t di = cfg.even_ifid, de = cfg.even_ex;
            if (!cfg.place && !(di | de)) {
                uint32_t n = 0;
                for (uint32_t d = 0; d < topo_.ndomains(); d++)
                    n += static_cast<uint32_t>(topo_.cpus_in(d).size());
                if (smt_mode_) {
                    n = 2 * topo_.allowed_sibling_pairs();
                    de = (n / 4) * 2;
                } else de = n / 2;
                di = n - de;
            }
            placed = cfg.place
                ? placement_.build_explicit(topo_, cfg.place)
                : placement_.build_even(topo_, di, de, smt_mode_ != 0);
        }
        if (!placed) return false;
        if (!placement_.configure_smt_units(topo_, smt_mode_ != 0)) return false;
        if (!placement_.reserve_runtime_roles(placement_.total_threads())) return false;
        if (placement_.ifid_threads().empty() || placement_.ex_threads().empty()) {
            std::fprintf(stderr, "placement needs at least one ifid and one ex thread\n");
            return false;
        }
        if (cfg.shards == Config::kShardsAuto)
            cfg.shards = cfg_default_shards(static_cast<uint32_t>(placement_.ex_threads().size()));
        return true;
    }

    bool init(const Config& cfg, const AofReplayPlan* aof_replay = nullptr) {
        if (placement_.total_threads() == 0) {
    uint32_t      size_ = 0;
    uint32_t      cap_ = Inline;
    uint32_t      offset_ = 0;     // byte offset within head_; only the head may be partial
};

class Client {
public:
    explicit Client(int fd) : fd_(fd) {
        rbuf_ = static_cast<char*>(std::malloc(kRbufInitial));
        rcap_ = kRbufInitial;
    }
    ~Client() { multi_session_destroy(multi_session_); std::free(rbuf_); }
    Client(const Client&) = delete;
    Client& operator=(const Client&) = delete;

    int  fd() const { return fd_; }
    int replace_fd(int replacement) {
        const int previous = fd_;
        fd_ = replacement;
        return previous;
    }

    // ---- read side -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
    char*    rbuf()      { return rbuf_; }
    uint32_t rlen() const { return rlen_; }
    uint32_t rpos() const { return rpos_; }

+int script_pcall_library(lua_State* state) {
+    ScriptContext context;
+    ScriptContext* current = &context;
+    // Keep the previous context slot rooted below the callable while the library runs. This
+    // works for both the temporary LOAD interpreter and an executor's persistent interpreter.
+    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &g_hook_context_key);
+    lua_rawget(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX);
+    lua_insert(state, -2);
+    const int saved = lua_gettop(state) - 1;
+    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &g_hook_context_key);
+    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &current);
+    lua_rawset(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX);
+    lua_sethook(state, instruction_hook, LUA_MASKCOUNT, kHookInterval);
+    int status = lua_pcall(state, 0, 0, 0);
+    lua_sethook(state, nullptr, 0, 0);
+    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &g_hook_context_key);
+    lua_pushvalue(state, saved);
+    lua_rawset(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX);
+    lua_remove(state, saved);
+    if (context.timed_out) {
+        if (status != 0) lua_pop(state, 1);
+        lua_pushliteral(state, "ERR function library exceeded the instruction limit");
+        status = LUA_ERRRUN;
+    }
+    return status;
+}

// Internal linkage is right for the counter itself -- prepare_write_key() below is its only
// writer, and it lives in this file's anonymous namespace with the rest of the transaction
// helpers. The READER that INFO calls cannot: it is declared in multi.h and defined out beyond
// this anonymous namespace, next to multi_task_owns_epoch().
std::atomic<uint64_t> g_exec_order_late{0};

enum class MultiPrepareWrite : uint8_t { Ready, Retry, Error };

MultiPrepareWrite prepare_write_key(Server& server, MultiExecState& state, Shard& shard,
                                    Slice key, uint64_t hash, uint32_t owner_thread_id,
                                    const void* watch_token = nullptr,
                                    std::atomic<uint32_t>* watch_refs = nullptr) {
    if (!watch_token) watch_token = &state;
    if (!watch_refs) watch_refs = &state.watch_refs;
    // THE FALSIFIER, and it must read ZERO. It asks EXACTLY the question the dispatch-time park in
    // ExLoop::execute() asks -- does this owner still hold an undecided record belonging to a
    // DIFFERENT logical unit of this connection? -- but asks it one step later, at install time.
    // The park is supposed to foreclose it completely, because only this owner thread may publish
    // into this owner's pending list, so nothing can appear between the dispatch check and these
    // installs. A non-zero reading is therefore not a statistic: it is proof that the park's
    // safety argument (NOTES-MULTIRACE.md §5) is false on this build, and that a transaction could
    // again clone a withdrawable candidate into an acknowledged write.
    //
    // It counts into its OWN counter, deliberately. Sharing atomic_exec_order_holds with the park
    // would make this arm unreadable: the park is non-zero BY DESIGN in exactly the runs that open
    // the window, so a sum can never be checked against zero and the falsifier would be inert --
    // the safety argument would break with no test going red. Split, each counter answers one
    // question: holds > 0 proves the hold fired, late == 0 proves it fired EARLY ENOUGH.
    // Not a Shard::Stats field because Shard's layout is locked at 1440 bytes; a namespace-scope
    // atomic costs nothing here, since the increment is on a path that is never taken.
    //
// anything larger is cheaper to retain through FlatStore's existing borrow registry.
struct ValueSlot {
    // Inline-copy cutover for gathered values. 24 was sized for integers; at 64B-class values it
    // pushed EVERY gather through the borrow path, whose bookkeeping (registry entry + segment
    // iov + release round-trip through the owner channel) costs more than a small memcpy — the
    // fork copies once at reassembly for exactly this reason (its OPT-1 keeps refs, but its
    // values cross as one copy into the reply). Borrow now reserves for genuinely large values
    // where wire zero-copy pays, mirroring the zc-min philosophy on the single-shard path.
    static constexpr uint32_t kInline = 1024;
    const char* ptr = nullptr;
    uint32_t len = 0;
    int32_t shard = -1;
    ValueKind kind = ValueKind::Nil;
    // Deliberately UNINITIALIZED: placement-new value-init was zeroing kInline bytes per slot per
    // op (8KB of memset per MGET-8 at the 1KB slot -- measured -34% at 64B values). Only the first
    // `len` bytes are ever written and read.
    char small[kInline];
};

+int script_pcall_library(lua_State* state) {

+    lua_pushvalue(state, saved);
+    lua_rawset(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX);
+    lua_remove(state, saved);

+        lua_pushliteral(state, "ERR function library exceeded the instruction limit");
+        status = LUA_ERRRUN;
+    }

+int script_pcall_library(lua_State* state) {
+    ScriptContext context;
+    ScriptContext* current = &context;
+    // Keep the previous context slot rooted below the callable while the library runs. This
+    // works for both the temporary LOAD interpreter and an executor's persistent interpreter.
+    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &g_hook_context_key);

+    lua_insert(state, -2);
+    const int saved = lua_gettop(state) - 1;
+    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &g_hook_context_key);
+    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &current);
+    lua_rawset(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX);
+    lua_sethook(state, instruction_hook, LUA_MASKCOUNT, kHookInterval);
+    int status = lua_pcall(state, 0, 0, 0);
+    lua_sethook(state, nullptr, 0, 0);
+    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &g_hook_context_key);
+    lua_pushvalue(state, saved);
+    lua_rawset(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX);
+    lua_remove(state, saved);
+    if (context.timed_out) {
+        if (status != 0) lua_pop(state, 1);
+        lua_pushliteral(state, "ERR function library exceeded the instruction limit");
+        status = LUA_ERRRUN;
+    }
+    return status;

bool tripwire_scatter_read_phase(const ScatterState& state) {
    if (!state.key_count || state.runtime_loading || state.kind == Kind::Script) return false;
    if (state.atomic_write) return false;
    if ((state.atomic_apply || state.atomic_pop || state.two_hop) && state.phase == 2) return false;
    return !sort_deref_gathering(state);
}

void xshard_tripwire_fragment_begin(const Task& task, Shard& shard, Op& op) {
    if (!atomic_tripwire_enabled() || !task.scatter || multi_task_tagged(task)) return;
    ScatterState& state = *task.scatter;
    if (!tripwire_scatter_read_phase(state)) return;
    ShardGroup* group = group_for(state, shard.id());
    if (!group) return;
    const uint64_t cut = state.atomic_pop && state.phase == 1 &&
                         state.pop_retry_snapshot != UINT64_MAX
        ? state.pop_retry_snapshot : state.snapshot;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < group->count; i++) {
        const uint32_t pos = state.key_order[group->begin + i];
        const KeyRef& key = state.keys[pos];
        const Slice bytes = op.arg(key.arg);
        atomic_tripwire_plain_begin(
            &state, &state, tripwire_scatter_slot(state, shard, pos), key.hash, cut,
            shard.store().atomic_tripwire_ticket(key.hash, bytes),
            shard.store().atomic_needs_version(key.hash, bytes));
    }
}

void xshard_tripwire_fragment_execute(const Task& task, Shard& shard, Op& op,
                                      bool plain_path, uint64_t cut) {
    if (!atomic_tripwire_enabled() || !task.scatter || multi_task_tagged(task)) return;
    ScatterState& state = *task.scatter;
    if (!tripwire_scatter_read_phase(state)) return;
    ShardGroup* group = group_for(state, shard.id());
struct KeyRef {
    uint64_t hash = 0;
    uint32_t arg = 0;
    int32_t shard = -1;
    KvObj* stable_object = nullptr;          // value-backed entry key identity
    KvObj* key_anchor = nullptr;             // uninstalled value ownership, freed with ScatterState
};

struct ResultHeap {
    std::string bulk;
    std::vector<std::string> members;
    std::vector<double> scores;
    // SORT's GET projection: one flag per row in `members`, 0 = the pattern resolved to nothing and
    // the row is a RESP null (an empty element under STORE). Empty for every other command.
    std::vector<uint8_t> present;
    // LCS's answer. The heap sidecar already exists for computed results, and growing it costs
    // the arena nothing -- it is allocated only by commands that reach ensure_result().
    LcsResult lcs;
};

struct RouteKey {
    uint64_t hash = 0;
    uint32_t arg = 0;
    int32_t shard = -1;
};

enum class XshardKeyUse : uint8_t { Read, SnapshotWrite };

struct XshardKeySpan {
    uint32_t first = 0;
    uint32_t count = 0;
    // The _RO forms are Readonly, exactly as Redis flags them: no AOF post-image pass and no
    // WATCH invalidation for an activation that cannot mutate. The atomic MVCC promotion still

    {"EVAL_RO",    3, -1, CmdFlags::Readonly | CmdFlags::CursorShard | CmdFlags::ScriptRoute |

};

void scripting_bind_server(Server* server) {
    g_script_server = server;
    if (server) g_instruction_limit = server->cfg().script_instruction_limit;
    if (!g_instruction_limit) g_instruction_limit = UINT64_MAX;   // 0 = unlimited
}

ScriptStats script_stats() {
    ScriptStats stats;
    stats.cached_scripts = g_scripts.size();
    stats.compile_hits = g_compile_hits.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
    stats.compile_misses = g_compile_misses.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
    stats.flush_generation = g_script_flushes.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
        "    Drop one library and every function it registered.",
        "LIST [LIBRARYNAME <name>] [WITHCODE]",
        "    Report libraries, their functions, descriptions and flags; WITHCODE adds sources.",
        "STATS",
        "    Report the running script (always nil here) and per-engine library/function counts.",
        "KILL",
        "    Terminate the running function. Functions are bounded by an instruction limit and",
        "    always terminate on their own, so this reports NOTBUSY.",
        "FLUSH [ASYNC|SYNC]",
        "    Drop every library. Both modes are synchronous here.",
        "DUMP",
        "    Serialize every library into a self-describing payload (TomoKV's own frame).",
        "RESTORE <payload> [FLUSH|APPEND|REPLACE]",
        "    Reload libraries from a payload produced by FUNCTION DUMP on this server.",
        "HELP",
        "    Print this help.",
    };
    reply_array_header(op.sink(), sizeof(lines) / sizeof(lines[0]));
    for (const char* line : lines) reply_simple(op.sink(), line);
}

void cmd_function(Shard&, Op& op) {
        auto* entry = static_cast<AtomicEntry*>(opaque);
        opaque = nullptr;
        if (!entry || !entry->plain() || entry->key_len != key.n ||
            Slice(entry->plain_key_data(), entry->key_len) != key) std::abort();
        entry->epoch = epoch;
        if (entry->plain_hash != hash) std::abort();
        KvObj* old = atomic_exchange_physical(hash, key, value);
        entry->parked()[0] = old;
        entry->count = 1;
        if (old) atomic_version_bytes_ += kvobj_size(old);
        if (value) atomic_gauge_sub(kvobj_size(value));
        value = nullptr;
        atomic_link_entry(*entry);
        atomic_read_epoch_ = epoch;
    }

    KvObj* atomic_install_transaction(uint64_t hash, Slice key, void*& opaque, KvObj*& value) {
        auto* entry = static_cast<AtomicEntry*>(opaque);
        opaque = nullptr;
        if (!entry || !entry->plain() || !entry->group_epoch || entry->key_len != key.n ||
            Slice(entry->plain_key_data(), entry->key_len) != key) std::abort();
        KvObj* old = atomic_exchange_physical(hash, key, value);
        entry->parked()[0] = old;
        entry->count = 1;
        if (old) atomic_version_bytes_ += kvobj_size(old);
        if (value) atomic_gauge_sub(kvobj_size(value));
        value = nullptr;
        atomic_link_entry(*entry);
        return old;
    }

    void atomic_finish_plain() {
        atomic_read_epoch_ = UINT64_MAX;
        atomic_read_origin_conn_id_ = 0;
    }

    KvObj* atomic_resolve(uint64_t hash, Slice key, uint64_t snapshot) {
        return atomic_resolve_internal(hash, key, snapshot, true).value;
    }
    // GROUP COMMIT IS TWO STEPS AND A READER MUST NEVER SEE THE FIRST WITHOUT THE SECOND.
    // A cross-shard group installs its versions on every owner while the shared epoch word still
    // reads zero (undecided ⇒ invisible), and only the last owner turns it into a ticket. That
    // ticket used to be drawn straight out of commit_seq_, so between the draw and the
    // `epoch.store(ticket)` two instructions later the sequence already named a commit whose
    // records still answered "undecided". A reader whose cut landed in that hole saw the group
    // for the fragments it read AFTER the store and missed it for the fragments it read BEFORE --
    // one MGET, two generations. The hole is nanoseconds wide and a preemption between the two
    // instructions makes it milliseconds wide; it produced exactly one torn MGET per ~1.1M
    // pipelined batches on the session-monotonicity hammer.
    //
    // So the visible read watermark is no longer the drawn sequence. Committers bracket
    // [draw, publish] in atomic_commit_inflight_, and whoever takes the count to zero republishes
    // the drawn sequence it read BEFORE its own decrement into atomic_commit_safe_: at that
    // instant every ticket at or below that value has already stored its epoch, because a
    // committer that had not would still be holding the count up. Readers load one word exactly
    // as before -- the cost is on the commit side, and it is two RMWs on a line commits already
    // own.
    uint64_t atomic_commit_reserve(uint64_t tickets = 1) {
        if (!tickets) std::abort();
        atomic_commit_inflight_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_seq_cst);
        return commit_seq_.fetch_add(tickets, std::memory_order_seq_cst) + 1;
    }
    void atomic_commit_publish() {
        // Loaded BEFORE the decrement on purpose: it is the value whose publication the count
        // still proves. Reading it after would let a ticket drawn by a newcomer ride in.
        const uint64_t drawn = commit_seq_.load(std::memory_order_seq_cst);
        if (atomic_commit_inflight_.fetch_sub(1, std::memory_order_acq_rel) != 1) {
            // Another committer is still between its draw and its store, so the watermark stays
            // where it is and every reader's cut stays below that undecided ticket. Counting it is
            // how the regression battery proves the guarded window actually opened.
            atomic_commit_windows_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
            return;
        }
        uint64_t safe = atomic_commit_safe_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
        while (safe < drawn &&
               !atomic_commit_safe_.compare_exchange_weak(
                   safe, drawn, std::memory_order_release, std::memory_order_relaxed)) {}
    }
    // Reserve a consecutive run under ONE commit bracket, then let the caller release-store every
    // decision word in its completion order before the safe watermark moves. The stall before the
    // first store is the atomic-ON use of DEBUG's shared hop delay: it widens the closed window on
    // demand, is zero in production, and the load is on an already-cold group/batch path. For a
    // one-ticket batch this is exactly the historical reserve/delay/store/publish sequence, while a
    // larger batch widens one common closed window.
    template <typename StoreTickets>
    uint64_t atomic_commit_batch(uint64_t tickets, StoreTickets&& store_tickets) {
        const uint64_t first = atomic_commit_reserve(tickets);
        const uint32_t stall = debug_hop_delay_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
        if (__builtin_expect(stall != 0, false)) debug_stall_us(stall);

+int script_pcall_library(lua_State* state) {
+    ScriptContext context;
+    ScriptContext* current = &context;
+    // Keep the previous context slot rooted below the callable while the library runs. This
+    // works for both the temporary LOAD interpreter and an executor's persistent interpreter.
+    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &g_hook_context_key);
+    lua_rawget(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX);
+    lua_insert(state, -2);
+    const int saved = lua_gettop(state) - 1;
+    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &g_hook_context_key);
+    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &current);
+    lua_rawset(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX);
+    lua_sethook(state, instruction_hook, LUA_MASKCOUNT, kHookInterval);
+    int status = lua_pcall(state, 0, 0, 0);
+    lua_sethook(state, nullptr, 0, 0);
+    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &g_hook_context_key);
+    lua_pushvalue(state, saved);
+    lua_rawset(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX);
+    lua_remove(state, saved);
+    if (context.timed_out) {
+        if (status != 0) lua_pop(state, 1);
+        lua_pushliteral(state, "ERR function library exceeded the instruction limit");
+        status = LUA_ERRRUN;
+    }
+    return status;
+}

template <typename T>
T* carve_at(char* base, size_t& off, uint32_t count) {
    if (!count) return nullptr;
    const size_t align = alignof(T);
    off = (off + align - 1) & ~(align - 1);
    T* result = reinterpret_cast<T*>(base + off);
    off += sizeof(T) * static_cast<size_t>(count);
    return result;
}

void init_arena_arrays(ScatterState& state) {

    state.groups = carve_at<ShardGroup>(base, off, state.group_cap);
    state.keys = carve_at<KeyRef>(base, off, state.key_count);
    state.key_order = carve_at<uint32_t>(base, off, state.key_count);
    if (has_values(state.kind, state.atomic_write))

    if (has_status(state.kind, state.atomic_write))

    if (state.atomic_write || state.atomic_apply)

uint64_t plain_read_cut(Server& server, const Op& op, uint64_t now) {

// pcall message handler. It must not change the error VALUE (Redis distinguishes a raised table
// with an `err` field from a raised string), so it only records where the throw happened: the
// first frame with a real source line, skipping the C frames of redis.call.
int script_error_handler(lua_State* state) {
    ScriptContext* context = lua_context(state);
    if (context) {
        lua_Debug frame;
        for (int level = 1; level <= 24; level++) {
            if (!lua_getstack(state, level, &frame)) break;
            if (!lua_getinfo(state, "Sl", &frame)) break;
            if (frame.currentline > 0) { context->error_line = frame.currentline; break; }
        }
    }
    return 1;
}

bool command_name_is(const CommandSpec& spec, const char* expected) {
    return std::strcmp(spec.name, expected) == 0;
}

bool script_name_whitelisted(const CommandSpec& spec) {
    // Deliberately explicit: command-table shape alone does not prove determinism (SPOP and
    // HRANDFIELD are both single-key). New commands remain unavailable until this list is audited.
    static constexpr const char* allowed[] = {
        "APPEND", "BITCOUNT", "BITPOS", "DECR", "DECRBY", "DEL", "EXISTS",
        "GET", "GETBIT", "GETRANGE", "GETSET",
            }
    watch_finalize_reservation(owned);
    // Read-only validation claims can coexist. A conflicting writer instead makes this EXEC
    // abort, including when it holds a blocking validation claim: waiting here permits cycles
    // between transactions that already reserved different keys on different owners.
    // Everything still on this key is an UNDECIDED reservation, and this transaction no
    // longer waits for it. Waiting was one half of the wait-for cycle, and it buys nothing that is
    // not already available here: a group holding a reservation on this key is a write to a key
    // this client watched, and "the group lands first" is a realizable serialization. Take it, and
    // this transaction must abort -- which is exactly what WATCH promises. The alternative reading
    // (the group lands after) is only reachable by waiting for a decision that may itself be
    // waiting on this transaction.
    if (auto pending = watch_reservations_.find(owned); pending != watch_reservations_.end())
        for (const WatchReservation& reservation : pending->second)
            if (reservation.token != token &&
                (reservation.mutates || (reservation.blocking && mutates))) {
                client->set_watch_dirty();
                stats_.watch_reservation_precommit_aborts++;
                break;
            }
    // A key that was alive when this client armed the WATCH and whose deadline has since elapsed is
    // a change, even when nothing has reaped it yet: redis aborts EXEC in that case whether the
    // removal came from its active cycle or is still pending. No command wrote the key, so the
    // reservation path never hears about it -- the armed deadline is the whole record.
    if (const auto watched = watchers_.find(owned); watched != watchers_.end()) {
        const int64_t now = now_ms_;
        for (const WatchEntry& entry : watched->second)
            if (entry.client == client && entry.generation == generation &&
                entry.expire_at_ms >= 0 && entry.expire_at_ms <= now) {
                client->set_watch_dirty();
                break;
            }
    }
    if (client->watch_generation() != generation || client->watch_dirty()) return true;
    if (!watch_append_reservation(owned, WatchReservation{
            token, epoch, aborted, refs, client, generation, mutates, /*blocking=*/true}))
        aborted->store(true, std::memory_order_release);
    return true;
}

bool Shard::watch_write_ready(Slice key, const void* token) {
    if (!has_watches()) return true;
    const std::string owned = watch_key_string(key);
    if (auto existing = watch_reservations_.find(owned); existing != watch_reservations_.end())
        for (const WatchReservation& reservation : existing->second)
            if (reservation.token == token) return true;

+int script_pcall_library(lua_State* state) {
+    ScriptContext context;

+    // works for both the temporary LOAD interpreter and an executor's persistent interpreter.

+    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &current);
+    lua_rawset(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX);
+    lua_sethook(state, instruction_hook, LUA_MASKCOUNT, kHookInterval);
+    int status = lua_pcall(state, 0, 0, 0);
+    lua_sethook(state, nullptr, 0, 0);
+    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &g_hook_context_key);
+    lua_pushvalue(state, saved);
+    lua_rawset(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX);
+    lua_remove(state, saved);
+    if (context.timed_out) {
+        if (status != 0) lua_pop(state, 1);
+        lua_pushliteral(state, "ERR function library exceeded the instruction limit");
+        status = LUA_ERRRUN;
+    }
+    return status;

+    lua_pushvalue(state, saved);
+    lua_rawset(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX);

// Ordinary one-key operations only enter this path when their key already has an MVCC record.
// Reads bind the current committed cut; writes first install a deep-cloned, freshly-ticketed
// version so collection handlers may continue mutating in place without touching a predecessor.
struct PlainForeignReadScope {
    struct Key { uint64_t hash; Slice key; };
    std::vector<Key> keys;
    bool active = false;
    bool poisoned = false;
};
bool xshard_plain_prepare(Server& server, Shard& shard, Op& op, uint64_t origin_conn_id,
                          PlainForeignReadScope& foreign_scope);
void xshard_plain_finish(Shard& shard, PlainForeignReadScope& foreign_scope);
uint32_t xshard_cleanup_shard(Server& server, Shard& shard, uint32_t budget = 8);
uint32_t xshard_cleanup_shard_at(Shard& shard, uint64_t floor, uint64_t cleanup_cutoff,
                                 uint32_t budget = 8);

}  // namespace tomo

+int script_pcall_library(lua_State* state) {
+    ScriptContext context;
+    ScriptContext* current = &context;
+    // Keep the previous context slot rooted below the callable while the library runs. This
+    // works for both the temporary LOAD interpreter and an executor's persistent interpreter.
+    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &g_hook_context_key);
+    lua_rawget(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX);
+    lua_insert(state, -2);
+    const int saved = lua_gettop(state) - 1;
+    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &g_hook_context_key);
+    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &current);
+    lua_rawset(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX);
+    lua_sethook(state, instruction_hook, LUA_MASKCOUNT, kHookInterval);
+    int status = lua_pcall(state, 0, 0, 0);
+    lua_sethook(state, nullptr, 0, 0);
+    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &g_hook_context_key);
+    lua_pushvalue(state, saved);
+    lua_rawset(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX);
+    lua_remove(state, saved);
+    if (context.timed_out) {
+        if (status != 0) lua_pop(state, 1);
+        lua_pushliteral(state, "ERR function library exceeded the instruction limit");
+        status = LUA_ERRRUN;
+    }
+    return status;

+int script_pcall_library(lua_State* state) {

+    int status = lua_pcall(state, 0, 0, 0);
+    lua_sethook(state, nullptr, 0, 0);
+    lua_pushlightuserdata(state, &g_hook_context_key);
+    lua_pushvalue(state, saved);
+    lua_rawset(state, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX);
+    lua_remove(state, saved);
+    if (context.timed_out) {
+        if (status != 0) lua_pop(state, 1);
+        lua_pushliteral(state, "ERR function library exceeded the instruction limit");
+        status = LUA_ERRRUN;
+    }
+    return status;

        state.final_reply == MultiFinalReply::ExecAbort ||

    }

    while (cursor < command_list.size()) {
        MultiCommand& command = *state.commands[command_list[cursor]];
        if (command.finished.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) {

        }
        const uint32_t stage = command.stage.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
        uint8_t& done = command.shard_done[shard_id];

            // The latter is a reusable table: source/gather/apply transitions rewrite it on the

                if (command.finished.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) continue;
                return MultiTaskResult::Retry;
            }
            if (done == stage + 1) {

                return MultiTaskResult::Retry;
            }

                notify_execute_source(shard, *command.op, command.notify_order_base);

            bool execute_child = true;
            if (command.scatter->atomic_pop && command.scatter->phase == 2) {
                ShardGroup* group = group_for(*command.scatter, shard.id());
                if (!group || group->count != 1) std::abort();
                const uint32_t pos = command.scatter->key_order[group->begin];
                const KeyRef& selected = command.scatter->keys[pos];
                const MultiPrepareWrite prepared = prepare_write_key(
                    server, state, shard, command.op->arg(selected.arg), selected.hash,
                    owner_thread_id, command.scatter, &command.scatter->watch_refs);

                if (prepared == MultiPrepareWrite::Error) {

                    command.scatter->aborted.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
                    execute_child = false;
                }
            }
